title: Stryker Neptune Surgical Fluid Management System – “Canister Full” or Level Sensor Errors
description: Troubleshooting guide for Stryker Neptune units displaying false “Canister Full” or level sensor errors, focusing on external causes before internal escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit is not actively connected to a patient before beginning troubleshooting. If in use, transition suction to wall vacuum or a backup device before continuing.

steps.title: Confirm the Message and Current Setup
steps.instructions: Verify the exact alarm message on the display. Determine which canister position is generating the error.

steps.title: Inspect the Canister Fluid Level
steps.instructions: Visually confirm the fluid level. If full or near full, properly dispose of contents per facility policy and replace with an empty canister.

steps.title: Remove and Re-seat the Canister
steps.instructions: Remove the affected canister. Inspect the bottom and rear connection points. Reinstall firmly, ensuring it is fully seated and locked in place.

steps.title: Inspect the Float Mechanism
steps.instructions: Check the internal float assembly inside the canister. Ensure the float moves freely and is not stuck in the “up” position. Look for coagulated debris or thick fluids restricting movement.

steps.title: Inspect Sensor Contact Area
steps.instructions: Examine the sensor interface area on the unit where the canister docks. Look for dried fluid, residue, or corrosion. Clean the external sensor contact area with approved disinfectant wipes (do not saturate).

steps.title: Swap Canisters Between Positions
steps.instructions: Move the suspected canister to another port (if applicable). Install a known-good canister in the original port.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Unit
steps.instructions: Turn the Neptune off. Wait 30 seconds. Restart and allow the system to complete self-test.

steps.title: Check for Signs of Fluid Intrusion
steps.instructions: Look for moisture, staining, or unusual odor near the canister ports. Check for alarm recurrence immediately after startup. If fluid intrusion into the internal sensor housing is suspected, do not continue operating the unit.

CCR.Complaint: Unit displaying ‘Canister Full’ alarm immediately after new empty canister installed.
CCR.Cause: Level sensor falsely detecting full condition in port #2. Float mechanism moved freely. Error remained with port after canister swap.
CCR.Resolution: Removed unit from service. Labeled Out of Service. Sent to shop for sensor evaluation and repair. Backup unit provided to OR.

helpfulDetails: Evidence of fluid residue at sensor interface
Whether alarm cleared after power cycle
Final device status (Returned to service or Sent for repair)

title: Stryker Neptune Surgical Fluid Management System – Low or No Suction
description: Troubleshooting guide for low or no suction on the Stryker Neptune system, focusing on external setup, tubing, canister configuration, and safety-first escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm suction is no longer actively required on a patient. Move suction to a backup wall suction source if needed. Do not troubleshoot while actively connected to a surgical field. Patient safety always comes first.

steps.title: Verify the Unit Is Powered On and Fully Booted
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit is powered on. Check for any alarm messages on the display. Ensure the unit has completed startup and is not in standby mode. If the system is not fully operational, suction will not engage.

steps.title: Confirm Suction Mode and Vacuum Level Settings
steps.instructions: Verify the suction channel is selected and activated. Check that vacuum level is set appropriately (not set to minimum or zero). Ensure the foot pedal (if used) is connected and functioning. Low settings can appear as “no suction” to clinical staff.

steps.title: Inspect All Tubing Connections
steps.instructions: Trace tubing from the surgical field to the Neptune inlet. Ensure all connections are fully seated and not loose. Check for cracked tubing, disconnected fittings, or split lines. Confirm the correct port is being used. Even a small air leak can significantly reduce vacuum performance.

steps.title: Check for Kinks or Occlusions
steps.instructions: Inspect suction tubing for: Kinks, Clots, Collapsed sections. Replace tubing if blockage is suspected. Mechanical obstruction is one of the most common causes of low suction.

steps.title: Inspect the Canister Setup
steps.instructions: Ensure the collection canister is: Properly installed, Locked into position, Not overfilled. Check that the lid and seals are intact. Confirm float shutoff has not engaged due to fluid level. An improperly seated canister or engaged float valve will stop suction.

steps.title: Verify Filter and Hydrophobic Barrier Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect for wet or saturated filters. Replace filters if moisture has breached the hydrophobic barrier. Wet filters can completely block vacuum flow.

steps.title: Listen for Pump Activity
steps.instructions: When suction is activated, listen for: Normal pump sound, Unusual grinding, No motor sound at all. If the motor does not engage, internal vacuum pump failure may be present.

steps.title: Check for Alarm Indicators
steps.instructions: Common alarms that affect suction: Full canister, Filter fault, Vacuum system error, Door or compartment not secured. Resolve any indicated alarm conditions and retest.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported Neptune unit had no suction during an OR case. Unit powered on but would not evacuate fluid.
CCR.Cause: Collection canister float shutoff engaged due to overfilled canister. Float valve blocking vacuum pathway.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced full canister, verified proper seating and seal. Tested suction at multiple vacuum settings. Unit functioning normally. Returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (Returned to Service or Sent to Repair)

title: Stryker Neptune Surgical Fluid Management System – Touchscreen / Control Panel Freezing
description: Troubleshooting guide for a Stryker Neptune Surgical Fluid Management System experiencing touchscreen or control panel freezing, focusing on external causes before internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure the Device Is Not Actively Connected to a Patient
steps.instructions: Before troubleshooting, confirm the unit is not in active use. If connected, transfer suction to another device first. Freezing during a case can create safety risk if suction control cannot be adjusted.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Power Cycle
steps.instructions: Many touchscreen freezes are software-related. Turn the unit off using the normal shutdown procedure. Wait at least 60 seconds. Disconnect from AC power. Reconnect power and restart the unit. A full power cycle clears temporary software faults and resets the control interface. If the touchscreen functions normally after restart, monitor for recurrence.

steps.title: Verify Stable Power Source
steps.instructions: Check if the unit is plugged directly into a wall outlet. Avoid extension cords or power strips. Test the outlet with an outlet tester or known working device. Inspect the power cord for damage. Unstable or fluctuating voltage can cause control board instability and display freezing.

steps.title: Inspect the Touchscreen Surface
steps.instructions: Check for fluid residue, cleaning chemical buildup, cracks in the screen, and physical pressure points. Wipe the screen with approved cleaning solution and lint-free cloth. Excess fluid infiltration around the bezel can interfere with capacitive or resistive touch response.

steps.title: Observe System Behavior During Freeze
steps.instructions: When freezing occurs, determine if the display remains lit, if physical buttons respond, if suction motors are still functioning, and if alarm tones are active. If suction continues but screen is frozen, the issue is likely interface-related rather than full system failure. If the entire unit becomes unresponsive, suspect deeper power or control board issue.

steps.title: Check for Environmental Factors
steps.instructions: Evaluate excessive OR humidity, fluid spills near the control panel, heat exposure, and whether terminal cleaning was recently completed. Moisture intrusion is a common cause of intermittent panel freezing.

steps.title: Check for Recurring Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine if freezing occurs only during high suction load, only during startup, or after prolonged use. Document pattern behavior. Intermittent freezing that worsens over time often indicates control board degradation.

steps.title: Inspect for Error Messages After Reboot
steps.instructions: After restarting, look for boot-up warnings, system faults, and software errors. Record any displayed codes before clearing them.

CCR.Complaint: “Touchscreen froze during procedure. Could not adjust suction level.”
CCR.Cause: “Unit powered on but touchscreen unresponsive. Power cycle temporarily restored function. Issue recurred after 20 minutes of operation.”
CCR.Resolution: “Removed unit from service. Verified stable power source. Labeled Out of Service and sent for further evaluation of control board/display assembly.”

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed – Will Not Power On
description: Troubleshooting guide for Stryker S3 hospital bed that will not power on, focusing on logical external power checks before internal component evaluation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Verify no patient is at risk due to bed position. If the bed is in use, safely transfer the patient to another bed before troubleshooting. Ensure brakes are engaged and side rails are secure before transfer.

steps.title: Verify AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is plugged directly into a known-good wall outlet. Test the outlet with another device (lamp, meter, or outlet tester). Avoid assuming the outlet is functional based on appearance alone. Why this matters: A tripped breaker or dead outlet is more common than internal failure. Checklist: Outlet tested; No extension cords in use; Hospital-grade receptacle verified.

steps.title: Inspect the Power Cord
steps.instructions: Check the entire length of the cord for cuts, pinch points, or exposed wiring. Ensure the cord is fully seated at the bed’s power inlet. Confirm the cord was not damaged during transport or housekeeping. If damage is observed: Remove the bed from service. Do not energize a compromised cord.

steps.title: Check for Battery Operation
steps.instructions: The S3 bed contains an internal battery backup. Unplug the bed and attempt to power on using battery. If the bed powers on via battery but not AC, suspect: Failed AC inlet; Internal fuse; Power supply issue. If the bed does not power on with battery: Battery may be fully discharged or failed. Checklist: Battery indicator lights observed; Charging status verified (if applicable).

steps.title: Inspect the Line Voltage Indicator (If Equipped)
steps.instructions: Some S3 configurations include indicator LEDs. Observe for any LED activity when plugged in. No lights at all may indicate: No incoming AC; Blown internal fuse; Failed power supply.

steps.title: Perform a Basic Reset
steps.instructions: Unplug the bed from AC power. Disconnect battery if accessible externally (do not disassemble). Wait 60 seconds. Reconnect AC power first, then battery. Attempt power-up again. Why this matters: Embedded controllers can occasionally latch and require a full reset.

steps.title: Inspect for Signs of Internal Electrical Failure
steps.instructions: Without opening the unit, check for: Burning smell; Unusual heat from control box; Visible fluid intrusion near electronics; Evidence of prior repair attempts. If any of these are present: Remove from service immediately.

steps.title: Confirm Control Lockout Is Not Engaged
steps.instructions: Some user reports of “dead bed” are actually control lockouts. Verify that side rail controls are not locked via nurse control panel. Attempt operation from multiple control locations. If functions operate from one panel but not another: Suspect local control board or wiring issue.

CCR.Complaint: Bed in Room 312 will not power on. No lights or movement from controls.
CCR.Cause: No AC power detected at wall outlet. Breaker was tripped. Bed functional once connected to verified outlet.
CCR.Resolution: Reset breaker, verified proper AC supply, confirmed bed powers on and all functions operate normally. Returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Final status: Returned to service / Sent to shop

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed – Hi-Low Actuator Failure
description: Troubleshooting guide for Stryker S3 hospital bed hi-low movement failures including actuator, power, and lockout evaluation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Transfer the patient to another bed if height adjustment is required. Do not work under the bed frame with a patient in the bed. Lower the bed to its safest position if possible. Hi-low failures can create fall risk or staff injury risk.

steps.title: Verify Power to the Bed
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is plugged into a known-good outlet. Test the outlet with another device. Check for illuminated power indicators on the bed. If equipped with battery backup, disconnect AC power and test hi-low on battery. Low voltage or a failed power supply can allow some functions to work while preventing high-load functions like hi-low from operating.

steps.title: Check for Lockout Activation
steps.instructions: Inspect side rail controls for hi-low lockout indicators. Verify that nurse panel lockouts are not active. Cycle lockout settings OFF and retest. Hi-low lockouts are commonly engaged during cleaning or transport.

steps.title: Test Multiple Control Points
steps.instructions: Test hi-low from patient pendant, side rail controls, and nurse control panel. If hi-low works from one control but not another, suspect a faulty pendant or localized control board. If hi-low does not work from any control, continue troubleshooting toward actuator or main control issues.

steps.title: Listen for Actuator Response
steps.instructions: When pressing hi-low, determine if you hear motor noise, a relay click, or complete silence. Clicking with no movement suggests possible actuator stall or mechanical binding. Motor noise without movement suggests possible stripped drive or linkage issue. Silence suggests possible power or control issue.

steps.title: Inspect Under-Bed Cabling
steps.instructions: Safely tip or access the base without a patient. Inspect hi-low actuator wiring harness. Look for pinched, stretched, or disconnected cables. Ensure connectors are fully seated. Check for corrosion at quick-connect fittings. Hi-low wiring runs through moving frame sections and is prone to stress damage.

steps.title: Inspect Mechanical Linkage
steps.instructions: Look for debris or obstruction in scissor frame. Verify no bent frame members. Check for transport damage. Ensure nothing is mechanically blocking movement. Do not disassemble the actuator.

steps.title: Check Battery Condition (If Equipped)
steps.instructions: Inspect battery for swelling or leakage. Measure voltage if applicable. Replace battery if it fails load testing. Weak batteries may allow light functions but not high-load lift motors.

steps.title: Evaluate Actuator Failure
steps.instructions: If power is confirmed, lockouts are cleared, controls are functional, wiring is intact, and no mechanical obstruction exists, likely causes include failed hi-low actuator motor, internal actuator limit switch failure, or main control board output failure. At this stage, escalation is appropriate.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reports bed will not raise or lower. All other functions operational.
CCR.Cause: Hi-low actuator not responding from any control panel. Power verified. Lockouts cleared. Wiring intact. Actuator silent during activation.
CCR.Resolution: Bed removed from service. Hi-low actuator replaced. Full function test performed. Bed returned to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed – Side Rail Control Panel Failure
description: Troubleshooting guide for Stryker S3 hospital bed side rail control panel failures, focusing on external power, lockout, and harness checks before internal component replacement.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Move the patient to another bed if possible. Ensure bed is in lowest position. Engage brakes. Confirm patient has alternate means of calling staff. Do not troubleshoot an electrical issue on an actively unstable patient.

steps.title: Confirm Bed Has Power
steps.instructions: Check if the bed is plugged into a known working outlet. Verify the outlet is tested and working. Confirm the main power switch is on (if equipped). Check for power indicator lights on the bed frame. The side rail panel requires system power from the bed control board.

steps.title: Test Other Bed Functions
steps.instructions: Using the main footboard control panel, attempt head up/down, bed height adjustment, and Trendelenburg if applicable. If all functions fail, suspect system-wide power or control issue. If footboard controls work but side rail does not, suspect localized side rail assembly issue.

steps.title: Check for Lockout Activation
steps.instructions: Verify caregiver lockouts are not active. Verify patient control lockouts are not active. Ensure controls are not disabled via nurse panel. A locked-out panel may appear failed when it is functioning properly.

steps.title: Inspect the Side Rail Panel Physically
steps.instructions: Look for cracked overlay, fluid intrusion, sticky buttons, loose mounting, or damaged membrane surface. Gently press each button and observe tactile feedback. If panel feels soft or spongy, membrane failure is possible.

steps.title: Inspect Side Rail Cable Routing
steps.instructions: Lower the side rail if safe and inspect the cable harness from rail to bed frame. Check for pinch points, frayed or exposed wires, and loose or partially seated connectors. Do not disassemble sealed electronics beyond connector-level inspection.

steps.title: Reseat External Connectors (If Accessible)
steps.instructions: Power down bed. Disconnect AC power. Reseat side rail connector if externally accessible. Restore power and retest. Do not access internal control boards beyond standard service access panels unless authorized.

steps.title: Check for Intermittent Operation
steps.instructions: Raise and lower rail slowly while observing panel. Slightly manipulate cable harness. If panel activates intermittently during movement, harness fatigue is highly likely.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported right side rail control panel not responding. Bed height and head functions inoperable from rail.
CCR.Cause: Verified bed powered. Footboard controls functional. Lockouts disabled. Inspection revealed intermittent response when articulating side rail. Suspected internal harness fatigue within rail assembly.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from service. Replaced right side rail control assembly. Tested all functions from rail and footboard. Returned bed to service after full operational check.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Exit Alarm Malfunction
description: Troubleshooting guide for Stryker S3 bed exit alarm failures, false alarms, and sensitivity issues using an external-first approach.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the alarm reliability is in question, move the patient to a safe, functioning bed. Implement alternative fall precautions per facility protocol. Do not perform troubleshooting while the bed is actively supporting a patient.

steps.title: Verify the Bed Exit Alarm Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed exit alarm is turned ON at the control panel. Check which sensitivity level is selected (e.g., low, medium, high). Ensure the alarm is properly armed after patient positioning.

steps.title: Confirm Proper Patient Positioning
steps.instructions: Ensure the patient is centered on the mattress. Verify the patient weight meets the detection threshold. Confirm linens are not excessively layered under the patient.

steps.title: Inspect Mattress and Surface Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm the mattress is the correct Stryker-approved surface for the S3. Verify no overlays or air surfaces have been added that could interfere. Remove any unauthorized pressure-relief pads temporarily to test alarm function.

steps.title: Check for Obstructions or Improper Mattress Installation
steps.instructions: Lift and reseat the mattress. Confirm the mattress is fully seated within the frame. Inspect for folded linens or objects between mattress and frame.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Bed
steps.instructions: Disconnect AC power. If equipped, disconnect battery briefly (if accessible externally). Reconnect power and allow full reboot. Re-arm the bed exit alarm and retest.

steps.title: Inspect Control Panel and Indicators
steps.instructions: Check for error codes on the display. Observe for intermittent alarm activation without patient movement. Confirm speaker function (audio not muted or failed). If available, test alarm volume adjustment.

steps.title: Check Bed Frame and Sensor Wiring (External Only)
steps.instructions: Inspect visible harness connections under the sleep deck (no disassembly). Look for pinched or damaged wiring. Check for recent maintenance that may have disturbed connections. Do not open control boards or remove deck panels beyond normal inspection.

steps.title: Functional Test (Without Patient)
steps.instructions: With mattress installed, apply distributed pressure manually. Arm the bed exit alarm. Gradually remove pressure and confirm alarm activation. Repeat test at different sensitivity levels. Do not test while the bed is actively supporting a patient.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reports bed exit alarm does not trigger when patient attempts to stand.
CCR.Cause: Mattress improperly seated in frame causing inconsistent pressure sensing.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated mattress, verified proper positioning, tested alarm at all sensitivity levels. Alarm functioning normally after correction.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (Returned to Service or Sent to Repair)

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed – Scale System Inaccuracy
description: Troubleshooting guide for inaccurate weight readings, zero failures, and scale fluctuations on the Stryker S3 hospital bed.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot scale accuracy with a patient on the bed. If weight accuracy is clinically necessary, transfer the patient to a verified scale first. Ensure brakes are engaged before performing any checks.

steps.title: Verify the Bed Is on a Level Surface
steps.instructions: The S3 scale system relies on load cells located at the frame. Uneven flooring or one caster elevated can cause inaccurate readings. Ensure all four casters are fully on the floor. Confirm the bed is not partially on a floor transition. Check that brakes are engaged. If necessary, relocate the bed to a known level surface and recheck.

steps.title: Ensure Nothing Is Touching the Bed
steps.instructions: External contact is one of the most common causes of scale inaccuracy. Check for IV poles resting on the floor, Foley bags hanging and touching the ground, bed linens caught between the bed and wall, oxygen tubing pulling against a wall, and the bed contacting a bedside cabinet or wall. The bed must be completely free-floating for accurate weight.

steps.title: Confirm Proper Zeroing Procedure
steps.instructions: If the bed was not zeroed properly, the displayed weight will be inaccurate. Remove all items from the bed surface. Ensure no linens or accessories are pressing against frame. Zero the scale according to normal operational procedure. Wait for weight to stabilize before adding patient. If zero fails repeatedly, power cycle the bed and attempt again.

steps.title: Check for Added or Removed Equipment After Weighing
steps.instructions: Common issue: staff remove SCD pump, wedges, or positioning devices without re-zeroing, or additional equipment is added after baseline weight. Confirm all equipment present during zero is still present, or perform a new zero with known configuration.

steps.title: Inspect Mattress and Deck Position
steps.instructions: Improper deck positioning may cause uneven load distribution. Lower bed to flat position. Ensure all deck sections are fully lowered. Confirm mattress is properly seated. Check that no deck actuator is partially engaged. Recheck weight after leveling bed.

steps.title: Inspect for Obvious Mechanical Issues
steps.instructions: Without disassembling, look for visibly bent frame, check caster assemblies for binding, listen for abnormal creaking when weight shifts, and observe if weight changes significantly when head section moves. Significant fluctuations during articulation may indicate load cell or internal wiring concerns.

steps.title: Power Reset
steps.instructions: If scale readings are erratic, disconnect bed from AC power. Remove battery power if accessible without disassembly. Wait 60 seconds. Reconnect and retest. This can reset scale controller communication.

steps.title: Cross-Check With Known Weight
steps.instructions: If possible, use a calibrated test weight or compare with another verified bed scale. If variance exceeds facility tolerance (commonly ±0.5–1 lb or per policy), further evaluation is required.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported bed weight reading 18 lbs higher than expected for patient.
CCR.Cause: IV pole was resting on floor and contacting wall, affecting scale reading.
CCR.Resolution: Freed IV pole from floor contact, re-zeroed bed scale, verified accurate reading within tolerance. Returned bed to service.

title: Stryker ProCuity Hospital Bed - Drive Motor Not Engaging
description: Troubleshooting steps for a Stryker ProCuity hospital bed that powers on but fails to move when drive controls are activated.

steps.title: Verify Bed Power Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is powered on and not in a low-battery condition. Check the main display for battery indicators or warnings. Ensure the bed is plugged into a known good wall outlet if battery level is low. Why this matters: The drive motor will not engage if battery voltage is below the safe operating threshold.

steps.title: Confirm Brake Status
steps.instructions: Verify central brake pedal position. Ensure the bed is in “neutral” or “steer” mode as appropriate for drive activation. Attempt to manually push the bed to confirm brake release. Why this matters: Engaged brakes mechanically prevent movement even if the drive motor attempts to activate.

steps.title: Verify Drive Enable Control
steps.instructions: Ensure the drive handle is fully extended and properly seated. Confirm staff are pressing and holding the drive enable switch while attempting movement. Inspect the drive handle cable (if applicable) for visible damage or pinching. Why this matters: The system requires an intentional enable signal before motor engagement.

steps.title: Inspect for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Check around all four casters and under the bed frame. Look for debris, IV tubing, cords, or floor obstructions. Confirm casters rotate freely. Inspect for string, tape, or debris wrapped around wheels. Why this matters: Mechanical resistance can prevent drive engagement or cause the system to inhibit motor activation.

steps.title: Check Bed Height and Position
steps.instructions: Lower the bed to a standard transport height. Ensure side rails are properly latched. Why this matters: Certain safety interlocks may prevent drive activation.

steps.title: Listen for Motor Activation
steps.instructions: Attempt to engage drive while listening closely. Do you hear a click, relay activation, or motor hum? No sound at all may indicate control or power issue. Clicking without movement may indicate mechanical coupling or motor failure.

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Power the bed off completely. Disconnect from AC power for 60 seconds. Reconnect and power back on. Why this matters: Resets may clear control lockouts or temporary faults.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Check for battery fault indicators. If available, swap with a known-good battery (per facility policy). Why this matters: Drive motors require higher current draw than basic bed functions. A weak battery may power electronics but not drive motors.

CCR.Complaint: Bed powers on but will not move when drive handle is engaged.
CCR.Cause: Brakes were engaged. Central brake pedal found in lock position preventing drive activation.
CCR.Resolution: Released brakes, verified drive motor engagement, and confirmed proper movement in forward and reverse. Bed returned to service.

title: Stryker ProCuity Hospital Bed - Battery Not Charging
description: Guide for troubleshooting a Stryker ProCuity bed that fails to charge its battery or shows low battery warnings.

steps.title: Verify Power Source
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is plugged into a known working wall outlet. Test the outlet with another device to confirm it has power. Why it matters: A dead outlet is the most common cause of a non-charging battery.

steps.title: Check Bed Connection to Charger
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed’s charging cable is fully inserted and free of damage. Inspect for bent pins, broken connectors, or frayed wires.

steps.title: Inspect Indicator Lights
steps.instructions: Look for charging LEDs on the bed or battery. Confirm that the charging light is on and steady. Flashing or no light can indicate battery or charger issues.

steps.title: Battery Seating
steps.instructions: Remove and reseat the battery to ensure proper contact. Listen or feel for a click to confirm secure installation.

steps.title: Swap with Known Good Battery
steps.instructions: If available, insert a charged battery from another ProCuity bed. If it charges, the original battery is likely faulty.

steps.title: Swap Charger/Cradle if Possible
steps.instructions: If a spare charger or docking station is available, test with the same bed. Confirms whether the problem is the charger or the battery/bed connection.

CCR.Complaint: Bed will not charge; battery warning light remains on.
CCR.Cause: Battery did not accept charge; charger and outlet confirmed functional.
CCR.Resolution: Battery removed, tested, and replaced with spare; defective battery labeled and sent for service.

helpfulDetails: Unusual sounds or heat: None noted
Final bed status: Replaced battery; bed operational

title: Stryker ProCuity Hospital Bed - Integrated Scale Drift
description: Troubleshooting guide for integrated scale drift on the Stryker ProCuity bed, focusing on external checks before service escalation.

steps.title: Verify Bed is on a Level Surface
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is placed on a flat, stable floor. Uneven surfaces can cause scale readings to drift.

steps.title: Check for Obstructions or Load on the Bed
steps.instructions: Remove any items on the mattress except the patient (if safe) or test weight. Make sure side rails or accessories are not applying uneven pressure.

steps.title: Inspect Power Connection and Battery Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is properly plugged in if the scale requires mains power. If the bed uses battery backup, ensure batteries are charged.

steps.title: Confirm Calibration Status
steps.instructions: Review the bed’s scale calibration logs if available. Some models allow a manual recalibration; follow manufacturer prompts.

steps.title: Perform a Zero or Tare Function
steps.instructions: Activate the scale’s zero/tare function with no weight on the bed. Observe if the scale stabilizes or continues to drift.

steps.title: Environmental Considerations
steps.instructions: Ensure temperature and humidity are within recommended ranges. Vibrations from nearby equipment can cause drifting readings.

steps.title: Swap Mattress or Mattress Support Pads
steps.instructions: If the bed uses specialized pads or mattress sensors, remove and reseat them. Check for uneven wear or compression affecting weight distribution.

CCR.Complaint: Integrated scale shows drifting weight readings and fails to stabilize.
CCR.Cause: Bed on uneven surface; calibration may be out of spec; potential mattress sensor issue.
CCR.Resolution: Verified surface, cleared obstructions, performed zero/tare, reseated mattress sensors; bed removed from service and sent for calibration/repair.

helpfulDetails: Any unusual noises or resistance from bed mechanisms
Final status before sending for repair

title: Stryker ProCuity Hospital Bed - Bed Exit Alarm False Alarms
description: Guide to troubleshooting false bed exit alarms on Stryker ProCuity beds, focusing on sensor, alignment, and connection checks before internal failure assumptions.

steps.title: Check Bed Occupancy Sensor Placement
steps.instructions: Ensure the sensor pad or mattress-integrated sensor is correctly positioned under the patient. Misaligned or bunched sensors can falsely detect a patient has exited the bed.

steps.title: Inspect Sensor Pad for Damage or Wear
steps.instructions: Look for cracks, tears, frayed wires, or moisture intrusion. A damaged pad may intermittently trigger alarms.

steps.title: Verify Bed Frame and Mattress Alignment
steps.instructions: Confirm mattress sits evenly on the bed frame without gaps that could interfere with the sensor. Check side rails are fully locked, as improper rail position can affect sensor readings.

steps.title: Check Electrical Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure the sensor cable is firmly connected to the bed controller. Look for bent pins or loose connectors.

steps.title: Test with a Known Good Sensor (if available)
steps.instructions: Swap the pad with a working one from a similar bed to see if the false alarms persist. If the issue resolves, the original pad is likely faulty.

steps.title: Inspect Bed Controller and Firmware
steps.instructions: Check for visible signs of damage or corrosion on the controller. Confirm the controller firmware is current per Stryker recommendations.

steps.title: Reproduce Alarm Conditions Safely
steps.instructions: With the bed unoccupied, observe if alarms trigger. If false alarms occur without a patient, suspect the sensor or controller.

CCR.Complaint: Bed exit alarm triggers repeatedly without patient leaving bed.
CCR.Cause: Sensor pad misaligned and/or cable connection intermittent.
CCR.Resolution: Checked pad placement, inspected connections, tested with known good pad. Issue persists → bed labeled Out of Service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Bed controller model and firmware version
Final bed status (Out of Service or returned to service after replacement)

title: Stryker ProCuity Hospital Bed - Touchscreen Lockups
description: Guide for addressing touchscreen freezes, lag, or unresponsiveness on Stryker ProCuity hospital beds with focus on external checks before internal repair.

steps.title: Check Power Supply
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is plugged into a working outlet or battery is charged. Verify indicator lights are on. Why: Touchscreen lockups can occur when voltage is low or unstable.

steps.title: Inspect Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: Check the connection between the touchscreen panel and the main bed controller. Look for loose connectors, bent pins, or visible damage. Why: A poor connection can cause intermittent touchscreen response.

steps.title: Reset the Bed Controller
steps.instructions: Perform a soft reset following the manufacturer’s instructions (usually power cycle). Wait 1–2 minutes before powering back on. Why: Temporary software glitches can cause touchscreen freeze; reset often clears them.

steps.title: Check for Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Ensure no strong magnets, mobile devices, or liquid spills are near the touchscreen. Clean the screen gently with a non-abrasive cloth. Why: Capacitive touchscreens can misread touches if the environment interferes.

steps.title: Test Other Bed Functions
steps.instructions: Adjust bed positions using manual controls (if available) or backup controls. Observe if lockups occur only on touchscreen or affect all functions. Why: Confirms whether issue is touchscreen-specific or more systemic.

steps.title: Update or Verify Software Version
steps.instructions: Check if the touchscreen/controller firmware is up to date. Why: Older firmware may have known touchscreen bugs; updating can resolve issues.

CCR.Complaint: Touchscreen freezes, unresponsive to input.
CCR.Cause: Controller reset and cable check indicate no external issues; software glitch or internal touchscreen failure suspected.
CCR.Resolution: Bed removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Bed powered via outlet or battery?

title: Stryker InTouch Hospital Bed - Scale Calibration Drift
description: Guide for troubleshooting Stryker InTouch hospital bed scale drift and inaccurate readings

steps.title: Verify Bed is on a Stable Surface
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is on a level, hard floor. Uneven flooring or caster locks not engaged can affect scale readings. Tilt or uneven load distribution can cause calibration drift.

steps.title: Check Caster Locks and Bed Frame Integrity
steps.instructions: Lock all casters and inspect for bent or loose frame components. Bed frame flex or movement can change the sensor load distribution.

steps.title: Remove All External Loads
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is empty of additional items (IV pumps, linens, equipment). Extra weight can skew calibration.

steps.title: Verify Power Source and Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm bed is connected to proper power or fully charged battery. Check for loose power connectors if using a wired scale module. Voltage fluctuations or intermittent power can cause erroneous readings.

steps.title: Perform Manufacturer-Recommended Scale Calibration
steps.instructions: Follow Stryker’s calibration procedure for the InTouch scale. If the procedure fails or drift occurs immediately after calibration, note error codes.

steps.title: Observe for Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Ensure no strong magnets, heavy electrical equipment, or vibration sources are nearby. Sensitive load cells can be influenced by electromagnetic interference.

CCR.Complaint: Bed scale drifting, inaccurate weight readings.
CCR.Cause: Calibration drift persists despite empty bed, level floor, and correct power.
CCR.Resolution: Performed calibration attempt; bed removed from service; sent to Stryker for evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Any unusual sounds or movement during weighing

title: Stryker InTouch Hospital Bed - Bed Exit Alarm Faults
description: Guide to troubleshooting bed exit alarm faults on Stryker InTouch beds, focusing on external checks before escalation.

steps.title: Verify Bed Power
steps.instructions: Check that the bed is plugged in and powered on. Confirm the display is active and shows normal startup messages. Low or intermittent power can cause alarm circuits to behave erratically.

steps.title: Inspect Bed Exit Sensor Pads / Mats
steps.instructions: Ensure sensor pads are correctly positioned under the mattress and not folded or bunched. Confirm connectors are fully seated at the bed and pad ends. Look for visible damage, frayed wires, or moisture. Misaligned or damaged pads often cause false or missing alarms.

steps.title: Check Bed Rails and Safety Settings
steps.instructions: Ensure side rails are in the proper position per facility protocol. Some alarm logic depends on rail positions. Confirm bed exit alarm is enabled in the user settings menu. Incorrect settings or rail positions can prevent the system from recognizing patient movement.

steps.title: Verify Mattress and Weight Thresholds
steps.instructions: Confirm that the mattress in use is compatible with the bed’s bed exit sensor system. If possible, simulate patient weight by pressing gently on the pad to see if the alarm triggers. The system uses pressure detection; incorrect mattress types or weight distributions can affect sensitivity.

steps.title: Inspect Cables and Connectors
steps.instructions: Check all sensor cables for secure connections and signs of wear or damage. Re-seat connectors at both the bed and sensor ends. Loose connections are a common source of intermittent alarms.

steps.title: Bed Software / Settings Check
steps.instructions: Access the bed’s configuration menu and verify alarm delays, sensitivity, and sound settings. Reset to default settings if persistent false alarms occur. Software misconfigurations can mimic hardware faults.

steps.title: Observe Alarm Behavior During Simulation
steps.instructions: With the bed empty, gently step on or lift the pad to verify alarm triggers. Note any irregularities such as delayed or absent alarms. Confirms the problem is consistent and reproducible before escalating.

CCR.Complaint: Bed exit alarm triggers intermittently, sometimes without patient movement.
CCR.Cause: Sensor pads improperly seated and one connector partially loose.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned sensor pads and re-seated all connectors. Alarm successfully tested and confirmed functional.

helpfulDetails: Test results (simulated weight or empty bed)

title: Stryker InTouch Hospital Bed - Brake Pedal Sensor Failure
description: Guide for troubleshooting Stryker InTouch bed brake pedal sensor issues, focusing on external checks before internal repair.

steps.title: Verify Bed Power
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is powered on and the battery is charged. Many sensors rely on active power to communicate; without power, the brake pedal signal may not register.

steps.title: Inspect Brake Pedal Mechanically
steps.instructions: Press each brake pedal and observe for smooth movement. Ensure nothing is physically blocking or jamming the pedal (linen, wheels misalignment, debris).

steps.title: Check Brake Pedal Sensor Connection
steps.instructions: Locate the sensor near the brake assembly. Verify the sensor harness is securely connected, not loose, pinched, or damaged.

steps.title: Test Brake Functionality Indicator
steps.instructions: Many InTouch beds have indicator lights on the control panel when brakes are engaged. Apply brakes and watch the indicator; if no response, suspect sensor or connection.

steps.title: Swap Pedal Sides (If Possible)
steps.instructions: If the bed has dual pedals and one side works, compare wiring and sensor functionality. This can help isolate whether the issue is the pedal, sensor, or wiring.

steps.title: Check for Error Codes on Bed Display
steps.instructions: Observe the InTouch display for any specific brake or sensor fault codes. Note codes for work order documentation.

CCR.Complaint: Bed does not register brake engagement; alarms indicate brake fault.
CCR.Cause: Brake pedal sensor unresponsive; mechanical pedal and wiring inspected and appear intact.
CCR.Resolution: Bed removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent for bench evaluation/repair.

helpfulDetails: Any error codes observed on the display

title: Stryker InTouch Hospital Bed - Control Panel Not Responding
description: Guide for troubleshooting a Stryker InTouch hospital bed when the control panel fails to respond to user inputs.

steps.title: Verify Bed Power
steps.instructions: Check that the bed is plugged in or battery is charged. Ensure outlet is live (use a known working device). Why: Control panel will not respond if the bed has no power.

steps.title: Check Main Disconnect / Battery Switch
steps.instructions: Locate the bed’s main power switch or battery disconnect. Cycle it off for 10 seconds and back on. Why: Resets control electronics and may clear temporary faults.

steps.title: Inspect Cables and Connectors
steps.instructions: Check ribbon cables, plugs, and connectors from the control panel to the main electronics. Look for loose, bent, or damaged connectors. Why: Loose connections can prevent the panel from responding.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the control panel for cracks, liquid spills, or visible damage. Clean any dirt or residue gently with a damp cloth. Why: Contamination or damage can interfere with button/touch functions.

steps.title: Test Other Control Inputs
steps.instructions: Try the side rail control or nurse control (if applicable). Confirm if they respond. Why: Helps determine if the problem is isolated to one panel or bed electronics.

steps.title: Cycle Power Again if Needed
steps.instructions: After inspection, power cycle the bed again to see if responsiveness returns.

CCR.Complaint: Control panel unresponsive; bed will not adjust height or position.
CCR.Cause: Bed has power, but panel does not respond to any inputs. External connections and other controls verified functional.
CCR.Resolution: Bed removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent for repair/bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Any visible panel damage or contamination noted
Bed status at time of removal

title: Stryker InTouch Hospital Bed - Motor Actuator Failure
description: Guide for troubleshooting non-responsive motor actuators on Stryker InTouch beds, focusing on external checks before repair.

steps.title: Verify Bed Power
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is plugged into a working outlet. Check the power cord for damage. Verify battery backup (if equipped) is charged. Why: Actuators require full voltage; low or absent power can mimic motor failure.

steps.title: Check Control Panel Functionality
steps.instructions: Confirm buttons and touch inputs are responsive. Cycle through all bed functions. Why: If the panel does not send commands, actuators will not move regardless of their condition.

steps.title: Inspect Bed Lock and Brake Sensors
steps.instructions: Ensure brakes are properly engaged/disengaged. Check indicator lights on brake sensors. Why: Some actuators will not operate if the bed is “locked” or if sensors detect unsafe conditions.

steps.title: Listen for Motor Noise
steps.instructions: Attempt to move the bed in a single function (e.g., raise head section). Listen for humming, clicking, or grinding from actuators. Why: No noise may indicate loss of power to actuator; unusual noise may indicate mechanical obstruction.

steps.title: Check Cables and Connections to Actuators
steps.instructions: Inspect actuator connectors for loose or disconnected wires. Look for pinched or damaged cables along the bed frame. Why: Loose or damaged wiring is a common cause of actuator failure.

steps.title: Swap or Test Actuator (if spare available)
steps.instructions: If possible, swap the suspected actuator with a known good one. Test function via the control panel. Why: Confirms whether the actuator itself is faulty or the issue lies elsewhere.

CCR.Complaint: Bed will not adjust positions; motor sounds but no movement.
CCR.Cause: Actuator did not respond to control panel commands; external power and connections verified.
CCR.Resolution: Bed removed from service; actuator labeled and sent for bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Audible motor noise noted: humming but no motion
Bed position at time of removal: Trendelenburg section stuck

title: Stryker 8800 Series Surgical Table - Hand Control or Foot Control Not Responding
description: Identifies causes of non-responsive hand or foot controls, including wiring, connection, battery, and obstruction issues before assuming internal control failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the table is not in use with a patient. If in use, safely transfer the patient to another table. Troubleshooting must never endanger a patient.

steps.title: Inspect Control Connection
steps.instructions: Verify that hand and foot controls are fully connected to their respective ports. Look for loose plugs, bent pins, or debris. Proper connection ensures signals are received by the table.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Examine cables and control surfaces for cuts, fraying, cracks, or worn buttons. Damaged controls can fail to transmit commands correctly.

steps.title: Test Alternate Control
steps.instructions: If available, try a known working hand or foot control. If it works, the original control is likely defective.

steps.title: Verify Power and Table Status
steps.instructions: Ensure the table is powered on and all indicator lights show normal operation. Some tables disable controls when in standby or fault conditions.

steps.title: Check Control Pairing (If Wireless/IR)
steps.instructions: For tables with IR or wireless hand controls, ensure pairing is correct. Re-pair controls according to manufacturer procedure if necessary.

steps.title: Observe Table Response
steps.instructions: Press each control function sequentially. Confirm movement or indicators respond. Record any functions that do not respond for documentation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported hand and foot controls unresponsive on Stryker 8800 table.
CCR.Cause: Loose hand control connection and partially worn foot control cable detected.
CCR.Resolution: Reconnected hand control, replaced foot control cable; table tested and fully operational.

title: Stryker 8800 Series Surgical Table - Table Will Not Power On
description: Identifies causes of no power, including power source, cord, battery, and connection issues before assuming internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the table is not in use with a patient. If in use, safely transfer the patient to another table before proceeding.

steps.title: Check Main Power Source
steps.instructions: Verify the wall outlet is live using a known working device. Ensure any circuit breakers controlling the outlet are on. Expected Outcome: Outlet provides proper voltage.

steps.title: Inspect Power Cord
steps.instructions: Check for visible damage, frays, or kinks. Ensure cord is fully seated in both the table and wall outlet. Expected Outcome: Table powers on or shows initial LED indicators.

steps.title: Verify Battery Condition (if equipped)
steps.instructions: Inspect battery charge level and connections. If battery is removable, reseat it. Attempt powering table from AC while battery is installed. Expected Outcome: Table powers on or shows charging indicator.

steps.title: Check Table’s Main Power Switch
steps.instructions: Ensure power switch is in the ON position. Toggle the switch off and on to test. Expected Outcome: LEDs illuminate and control panel becomes active.

steps.title: Examine Fuses and Circuit Protection
steps.instructions: Check accessible fuses for continuity. Replace blown fuses with correct rating only. Expected Outcome: Table responds to power.

steps.title: Test Control Panel Indicators
steps.instructions: Look for any error lights or messages. Document unusual indicators for service escalation. Expected Outcome: Normal startup sequence begins.

CCR.Complaint: Table will not power on in the OR.
CCR.Cause: Power cord and outlet verified; table does not respond to main power or battery input.
CCR.Resolution: Table removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested with multimeter or known device
Any LED indicators or error codes noted

title: Stryker 8800 Series Surgical Table - Hydraulic System Leaks or Slow Movement
description: Identifies causes of hydraulic leaks or sluggish table movement, including fluid level, hose integrity, valve operation, and obstruction issues before assuming major internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the table is not supporting a patient. If in use, safely transfer the patient to another table. Never operate a leaking hydraulic system under a patient.

steps.title: Inspect for Visible Leaks
steps.instructions: Check under the table, around cylinders, hoses, and fittings for fluid leaks. Leaks can reduce pressure and slow movement; visible fluid indicates the source.

steps.title: Check Hydraulic Fluid Level
steps.instructions: Locate the hydraulic reservoir and verify fluid level. Low fluid can cause sluggish movement. Refill with manufacturer-approved hydraulic fluid if low.

steps.title: Examine Hoses and Fittings
steps.instructions: Look for kinks, cracks, or loose connections in hydraulic lines. Tighten fittings or replace damaged hoses to restore flow and prevent leaks.

steps.title: Test Table Movement Without Load
steps.instructions: Operate the table without a patient to see if movement improves. Slow or jerky operation may indicate internal valve restriction or air in the system.

steps.title: Check for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Ensure no debris or mechanical obstruction is interfering with hydraulic cylinder movement. Clear any blockages before testing again.

steps.title: Listen and Observe for Abnormal Sounds
steps.instructions: Hissing, gurgling, or inconsistent movement can indicate internal leaks or air in the hydraulic system. Document observations for repair escalation.

CCR.Complaint: Surgical table moves slowly and has visible hydraulic fluid beneath base.
CCR.Cause: Low hydraulic fluid and minor leak at cylinder fitting.
CCR.Resolution: Topped off hydraulic fluid, tightened loose fittings, tested table movement.

title: Stryker 8800 Series Surgical Table - Table Drift or Position Instability
description: Identifies causes of table drift or unstable positioning, including hydraulic, lock, load, and control issues before assuming internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the table is not supporting a patient. If in use, safely transfer the patient to another table or stretcher.

steps.title: Check Table Locks
steps.instructions: Inspect all mechanical locks or brakes for engagement. Ensure the table is fully locked in the neutral position. Drift can occur if locks are not set properly.

steps.title: Inspect Power and Hydraulics
steps.instructions: Verify the table is powered on and connected to a stable outlet or battery. Check for any visible hydraulic fluid leaks, low fluid levels, or damaged hoses. Low fluid can reduce stability.

steps.title: Examine Load Distribution
steps.instructions: Remove any heavy attachments or surgical accessories. Uneven load can cause drift or instability. Confirm table is level on the floor.

steps.title: Test Control Functionality
steps.instructions: Operate the table through hand and foot controls. Observe movement in each axis. Intermittent response may indicate a control input or connection issue.

steps.title: Check for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect under-table components and rails for objects interfering with movement. Even small debris can affect stability.

steps.title: Observe for Alarms or Indicators
steps.instructions: Note any warning lights, error codes, or unusual sounds during movement. Document these for repair escalation.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the table drifts when trying to hold position during surgery.
CCR.Cause: External checks revealed no lock engagement and minor hydraulic fluid level reduction.
CCR.Resolution: Adjusted locks and topped off hydraulic fluid; table tested stable in all positions.

title: Stryker 8800 Series Surgical Table - Trendelenburg or Lateral Tilt Not Functioning
description: Identifies causes of non-functioning Trendelenburg or lateral tilt, including control, actuator, safety lock, and load issues before assuming internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the table is not supporting a patient. If in use, safely transfer the patient to another table before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Power Source
steps.instructions: Verify the table is plugged in and the circuit is live. Check for tripped breakers or GFCI outlets. Without proper power, tilt motors will not operate.

steps.title: Inspect Hand Control / Pendant
steps.instructions: Ensure the hand control or pendant is connected securely. Operate other movements (height, longitudinal) to verify responsiveness. If the hand control is unresponsive, this may be the cause.

steps.title: Examine Foot Control (If Equipped)
steps.instructions: Some tilt functions may be activated via foot control. Confirm foot pedal is fully engaged and connections are secure.

steps.title: Check Safety Locks / Brakes
steps.instructions: Verify that all brakes or locks are disengaged. Tilt functions are often inhibited when brakes are engaged.

steps.title: Observe Table Load and Balance
steps.instructions: Remove any heavy attachments or accessories. Tilt motors may fail to operate under excessive load or if the table is unbalanced.

steps.title: Listen for Motor Response
steps.instructions: While commanding a tilt, listen for motor noise. No sound may indicate electrical or control issues; abnormal sounds may indicate mechanical obstruction.

steps.title: Inspect Wiring and Actuators (External Checks Only)
steps.instructions: Look for visible pinched or disconnected cables at the base of the table. Ensure actuator rods or tilt mechanisms are free of obstruction.

steps.title: Test with Minimal Load
steps.instructions: Operate Trendelenburg and lateral tilt without patient or heavy attachments. Functioning with minimal load may indicate a load or obstruction issue rather than internal motor failure.

CCR.Complaint: Trendelenburg and lateral tilt do not respond to hand or foot controls.
CCR.Cause: Tilt motors did not respond; external inspection revealed no loose connections or obstructions.
CCR.Resolution: Table removed from service and labeled Out of Service for repair.

helpfulDetails: No abnormal sounds or heat detected

title: Stryker FL28 / FL36 Hospital Bed - Hi-Lo Actuator Failure or Slow Movement
description: Identifies causes of hi-lo actuator failure or slow movement, including power, battery, cabling, and obstruction issues before assuming actuator motor failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Verify the bed is unoccupied or move the patient to another bed. Lock bed brakes to prevent unexpected movement during troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Power Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is plugged into a working outlet. Test the outlet with another device. Expected Outcome: Bed powers on and hand/foot controls light up.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Backup
steps.instructions: Verify the bed’s internal battery is charged. Replace or recharge battery if voltage is low. Expected Outcome: Battery supports actuator movement without slow response.

steps.title: Examine Hand/Foot Controls
steps.instructions: Operate the hi-lo controls from both panels. Swap with a known working control if available. Expected Outcome: If control is faulty, actuator responds when using alternate panel.

steps.title: Inspect Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: Check actuator cables for pinched, disconnected, or damaged wires. Ensure connectors are fully seated. Expected Outcome: Secure connections restore normal actuator function.

steps.title: Check for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect bed frame and undercarriage for anything restricting actuator movement. Remove objects or reposition mattress if needed. Expected Outcome: Actuator moves smoothly without mechanical blockage.

steps.title: Test Bed Functions
steps.instructions: Operate all positions (hi-lo, Trendelenburg, backrest) to verify movement. Listen for unusual sounds or motor strain. Expected Outcome: Movement returns to normal speed and range.

CCR.Complaint: Hi-lo actuator slow to respond or not functioning.
CCR.Cause: Battery low and actuator cable partially disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Recharged battery, secured cable connections; actuator movement restored.

title: Stryker FL28 / FL36 Hospital Bed - Bed Exit Alarm False Alarms
description: Identifies causes of false bed exit alarms, including sensor misalignment, patient movement, wiring, or configuration errors before assuming sensor failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient is safely in another bed or seated in a chair while troubleshooting. False alarms can distract staff and create unsafe conditions.

steps.title: Inspect Sensor Pad Position
steps.instructions: Check that the bed exit sensor pad is properly positioned under the mattress as per manufacturer instructions. Misalignment can trigger false alarms. Expected outcome: pad lies flat and centered; false alarms should reduce.

steps.title: Verify Mattress Compatibility
steps.instructions: Ensure the mattress in use is compatible with the sensor pad. Overly thick or foam mattresses may affect sensor activation. Expected outcome: correct mattress allows proper sensor function.

steps.title: Check Bed Side Rails and Accessories
steps.instructions: Ensure side rails are fully up or down as required. Certain accessory positions can influence sensor detection. Expected outcome: proper configuration reduces unnecessary alarms.

steps.title: Examine Wiring and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the sensor pad cable for pinching, fraying, or loose connectors at the bed and headboard junction. Tighten or reseat as necessary. Expected outcome: secure connections; false alarms may resolve.

steps.title: Review Bed Settings and Alarm Configuration
steps.instructions: Check the bed’s control panel for alarm sensitivity settings. Adjust sensitivity according to patient size and mobility. Expected outcome: alarm triggers only when patient exits the bed.

steps.title: Test with Simulated Patient Movement
steps.instructions: With no patient, simulate movement on the sensor pad to ensure alarms respond correctly without triggering falsely. Expected outcome: alarms function normally; no false triggers.

CCR.Complaint: Bed exit alarm repeatedly triggered without patient movement.
CCR.Cause: Sensor pad misaligned under mattress and wiring connector loose.
CCR.Resolution: Pad repositioned, connector reseated, and alarm sensitivity adjusted; tested successfully.

helpfulDetails: Alarm sensitivity settings before and after adjustment
Any unusual noises or indicator lights

title: Stryker FL28 / FL36 Hospital Bed - Side Rail Control Panel Failure
description: Identifies causes of side rail control panel failure, including power, connection, or configuration issues before assuming internal panel failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Verify the patient is safely out of the bed or in a stable position. Never troubleshoot controls while a patient is in bed to prevent accidental movement.

steps.title: Check Bed Power
steps.instructions:
Confirm the bed is plugged in or battery is charged.
Expectation: Bed functions on other controls if power is adequate.

steps.title: Inspect Side Rail Locking Mechanism
steps.instructions:
Ensure the side rail is fully latched; some panels are disabled when not fully engaged.
Expectation: Panel should respond once the rail is correctly positioned.

steps.title: Examine Wiring Connections
steps.instructions:
Inspect wiring harness between side rail panel and bed electronics for loose or damaged connectors.
Expectation: Re-seating or securing connectors restores panel functionality.

steps.title: Test Alternate Controls
steps.instructions:
Operate bed using the foot panel or nurse control.
Expectation: If alternate controls work, issue is isolated to side rail panel.

steps.title: Check Panel for Visible Damage
steps.instructions:
Look for cracks, water damage, or stuck buttons.
Expectation: Minor debris removal may restore function; physical damage requires replacement.

steps.title: Software/Reset Check
steps.instructions:
If bed supports a reset or power cycle, perform it per facility protocol.
Expectation: Panel may regain responsiveness after reset.

CCR.Complaint: Side rail control panel unresponsive when patient attempted adjustment.
CCR.Cause: Loose wiring harness found between side rail panel and main electronics.
CCR.Resolution: Re-seated connector; panel restored full function.

helpfulDetails: Side rail fully engaged and locked

title: Stryker FL28 / FL36 Hospital Bed - Scale Inaccuracy or Drift
description: Addresses inaccurate weight readings or drifting scales due to power, calibration, connection, or environmental factors.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is unoccupied or the patient is safely moved to another bed. Never attempt scale calibration or testing with a patient on the bed if readings may be inaccurate.

steps.title: Check Bed Level and Placement
steps.instructions: Ensure the bed is on a flat, stable surface. Uneven floors can cause scale drift or incorrect weight readings. Adjust bed position if needed.

steps.title: Verify Power and Battery Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is connected to a functional power source. Check battery backup; low battery can affect scale accuracy. Observe scale display behavior after power cycling.

steps.title: Inspect Cables and Connectors
steps.instructions: Examine any scale-specific cabling between the bed frame and control module. Look for loose connections, frayed wires, or corrosion. Secure or replace as needed.

steps.title: Check for Interference or Load Issues
steps.instructions: Remove any non-patient weight (linens, equipment) from the bed. Ensure side rails, IV poles, or accessories are not causing uneven load.

steps.title: Perform Scale Calibration or Tare Function
steps.instructions: Use the bed’s calibration or zeroing function per manufacturer instructions. Confirm scale reads “0” when bed is empty. Place a known weight (e.g., calibration test weight) to verify accuracy.

steps.title: Observe Indicator Lights or Error Codes
steps.instructions: Check for scale or system error indicators on the control panel. Document any persistent warnings or abnormal readings.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported bed scale reading fluctuates and drifts over time.
CCR.Cause: Bed on uneven floor; calibration not recently performed; minor connector looseness observed.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned bed, secured cables, recalibrated scale; verified accuracy with test weight; returned to service.

title: Stryker FL28 / FL36 Hospital Bed - Power Supply or Battery Backup Failure
description: Identifies causes of bed power loss or battery backup failure, including outlet, cabling, battery, and fuse issues before assuming internal electronics failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient is safely transferred or the bed is unoccupied. Never work on power systems with a patient in the bed.

steps.title: Check Main Power Source
steps.instructions: Verify the wall outlet is live using a known working device. Ensure the bed’s power cord is fully seated in the outlet. Expected outcome: Bed powers on when plugged into a confirmed live outlet.

steps.title: Inspect Power Cord and Connections
steps.instructions: Examine the power cord for cuts, frays, or damage. Check connections at the bed and at the control module. Expected outcome: No visible damage; cord firmly connected.

steps.title: Verify On-Board Fuses or Circuit Breakers
steps.instructions: Locate the bed’s power module fuses/circuit breakers. Replace blown fuses or reset tripped breakers. Expected outcome: Bed powers on or shows normal status indicators.

steps.title: Check Battery Backup
steps.instructions: If bed has battery backup, verify battery is installed and properly seated. Observe battery charge status indicators if available. Expected outcome: Bed operates on battery when unplugged; indicator shows charge.

steps.title: Swap or Test Battery
steps.instructions: If bed still fails to power on, try a known good battery (if available). Observe if bed powers on normally. Expected outcome: Bed powers on with a known good battery.

steps.title: Observe Bed Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on/off cycles should be normal; no unexpected shutdowns or indicator lights signaling faults. Note any unusual sounds or heat from the power module.

CCR.Complaint: Bed loses power intermittently, fails to operate on battery.
CCR.Cause: Battery was discharged and power cord had a loose connection.
CCR.Resolution: Secured power cord and replaced battery; bed powers on normally.

helpfulDetails: Battery presence, seating, and charge status

title: Stryker System 7 Power Tools - Battery not charging or holding charge
description: Identifies causes when batteries fail to charge, discharge quickly, or are not recognized by the charger, affecting tool readiness for surgical procedures.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm no active surgery is dependent on the affected tool. Move patient care to a backup system or alternate tools if necessary.

steps.title: Inspect Power Source and Charger
steps.instructions: Verify the wall outlet is live using a multimeter or known-working device. Check the charger for damage, loose connections, or blown fuses. Expected Outcome: Charger powers on and shows normal indicator lights.

steps.title: Examine Battery and Contacts
steps.instructions: Remove the battery and inspect contacts for dirt, corrosion, or damage. Clean contacts with a lint-free cloth or isopropyl alcohol if needed. Expected Outcome: Clean, undamaged contacts improve connection reliability.

steps.title: Swap with Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: Test the charger with a fully charged, known-good battery. If it charges correctly, the issue is likely with the original battery. Expected Outcome: Confirms whether the battery or charger is at fault.

steps.title: Test Battery on System Tool
steps.instructions: Insert the battery into a System 7 tool and verify operation. If the tool shows low battery or fails to operate, the battery may be defective. Expected Outcome: Tool operates normally with a functioning battery.

steps.title: Check Battery Age and Cycle Count
steps.instructions: Review battery label or system log for age and number of charge cycles. Batteries beyond manufacturer’s recommended life may not hold charge. Expected Outcome: Identify batteries requiring replacement due to end-of-life.

steps.title: Inspect Charger Indicator Lights and Error Codes
steps.instructions: Refer to Stryker documentation for specific charger LED/error behavior. Expected Outcome: Visual indicators may point to battery or charger faults.

CCR.Complaint: Battery fails to charge and does not hold power.
CCR.Cause: Battery contacts were corroded and battery exceeded manufacturer’s cycle life.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned contacts, replaced battery with a new, fully charged unit; verified operation on tool.

helpfulDetails: Final device status: operational or replaced

title: Stryker System 7 Power Tools - Handpiece not recognized by console
description: Identifies causes when the handpiece is not detected by the console, preventing motor operation and delaying surgical readiness.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm no active surgery is using the affected handpiece. Move patient to another tool or procedure if necessary.

steps.title: Inspect Handpiece Connection
steps.instructions: Check that the handpiece is fully seated in the console port. Improper connection prevents recognition. Expected: console acknowledges the handpiece.

steps.title: Check for Debris or Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect handpiece and console connectors for debris, corrosion, or bent pins. Clean with approved wipes if needed. Expected: clear contact surfaces.

steps.title: Swap Handpiece or Console Port
steps.instructions: If available, connect a known-working handpiece to the console, or the affected handpiece to a different console port. This identifies faulty handpiece or port. Expected: working handpiece is recognized; faulty component isolated.

steps.title: Inspect Cable Integrity
steps.instructions: Check the cable between the console and handpiece for visible damage, kinks, or loose connectors. Expected: no visible defects; console recognizes handpiece.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Console
steps.instructions: Turn console off, wait 10 seconds, and power back on. Reconnect handpiece. Expected: console recognizes handpiece after reboot.

steps.title: Check Software/Console Updates
steps.instructions: Ensure console firmware is current; outdated firmware may prevent recognition. Follow manufacturer instructions for update. Expected: handpiece recognized post-update.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the handpiece was not recognized by the System 7 console.
CCR.Cause: Connector pins on the handpiece showed slight contamination; cable and console ports verified functional.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned handpiece connector; confirmed recognition after reconnection; console returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Console port functionality (tested with another handpiece)

title: Stryker System 7 Power Tools - Motor failure or reduced torque
description: Identifies causes when the motor operates weakly or intermittently, impacting surgical performance and procedural efficiency.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm no active surgery is dependent on the affected tool. Move patient to an alternate power tool to prevent procedural delay.

steps.title: Verify Power Source
steps.instructions: Check battery charge level; ensure fully charged and seated correctly. Swap with a known good battery if available. Expected Outcome: Motor should operate at full torque with a good battery.

steps.title: Inspect Handpiece Connection
steps.instructions: Remove and reconnect handpiece to console, ensuring pins align and no debris is present. Check for corrosion, bent pins, or damaged connectors. Expected Outcome: Proper connection allows full motor function.

steps.title: Check Motor Function Without Load
steps.instructions: Activate motor in air (no surgical load) to observe speed and torque. Expected Outcome: Motor should run smoothly; stuttering indicates possible motor or handpiece issue.

steps.title: Test Alternate Handpiece or Console Port
steps.instructions: Swap with a different handpiece or console port to isolate the problem. Expected Outcome: If torque returns to normal, original handpiece or port may be faulty.

steps.title: Examine Settings and Mode Selection
steps.instructions: Verify torque, speed, and mode settings on the console match intended surgical requirements. Expected Outcome: Misconfigured settings can mimic reduced torque.

steps.title: Observe for Unusual Sounds or Heat
steps.instructions: Listen for grinding, clicking, or abnormal vibration. Check for excessive warmth after brief use. Expected Outcome: Unusual behavior can indicate internal motor wear or damage.

CCR.Complaint: Motor on System 7 handpiece operates weakly or stalls under load.
CCR.Cause: Battery and handpiece connection verified; motor performance remains below expected torque.
CCR.Resolution: Tool removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Final device status: Out of Service

title: Stryker System 7 Power Tools - Charger Dock Not Recognizing Batteries
description: Identifies causes when the charger fails to detect batteries, preventing charging and delaying surgical readiness.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm no surgery is currently dependent on the affected battery. Move patient to a different fully charged tool if necessary.

steps.title: Inspect Charger Dock and Battery Contacts
steps.instructions: Check for dirt, corrosion, or debris on battery terminals and dock connectors. Clean with a dry lint-free cloth or isopropyl alcohol. Expected outcome: Clean connections allow proper recognition.

steps.title: Verify Battery Orientation and Seating
steps.instructions: Ensure battery is fully inserted and clicks into place. Sometimes partial insertion prevents detection. Expected outcome: Proper seating triggers charging indicator.

steps.title: Test With a Known Good Battery
steps.instructions: Insert a fully charged, functioning battery into the dock. If recognized, the issue may be with the original battery. Expected outcome: Good battery recognized; original battery may be defective.

steps.title: Test Dock With Another Charger or Outlet
steps.instructions: Plug dock into a verified working outlet or another compatible charger. Swap if available to rule out power supply or outlet issues. Expected outcome: Dock powers up; indicator lights function.

steps.title: Observe Charger Indicator Lights
steps.instructions: Check if LEDs flash, stay solid, or remain off. Different patterns indicate dock status or error codes (per console guidance). Expected outcome: Indicator confirms functional dock or signals a fault.

steps.title: Check Firmware and Console Recognition (If Dock Connected to Console)
steps.instructions: Ensure console recognizes the dock if it is networked or communicates status. Expected outcome: Console confirms dock status; software errors are ruled out.

CCR.Complaint: Charger dock does not recognize any System 7 batteries.
CCR.Cause: Charger contacts dirty and one battery partially defective.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned dock contacts, verified with known good battery; defective battery removed and replaced.

helpfulDetails: Final device status: functional or sent for repair

title: Stryker System 7 Power Tools - Console Error Codes or Self-Test Failure
description: Identifies causes when the console displays error codes or fails self-test, preventing safe use and delaying surgical readiness.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm no patient is dependent on the affected tool. Move patient to a backup tool to prevent procedural delays or risk.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the console is properly seated on the charging dock or power base. Ensure wall outlet is live and tested with a known-working device. Inspect AC/DC adapters and cables for damage. Expected outcome: Console powers on without error; if not, proceed.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Status
steps.instructions: Remove and reseat batteries in the console. Ensure batteries are charged and functional. Why it matters: Low or faulty batteries can cause self-test failures.

steps.title: Perform Console Reset / Power Cycle
steps.instructions: Turn off console, wait 30 seconds, then power on. Expected outcome: Console completes self-test; error code clears if transient fault.

steps.title: Check for Visible Damage or Debris
steps.instructions: Inspect connector pins, ports, and the console housing. Remove any debris or corrosion. Expected outcome: Physical connection issues corrected; console may now pass self-test.

steps.title: Review Error Code Documentation
steps.instructions: Compare displayed codes to Stryker System 7 error code list (internal CE reference). Identify codes indicating external vs. internal failure.

steps.title: Swap with Known-Good Console (if available)
steps.instructions: Place the console on the same dock and power source. Expected outcome: Determines whether error is console-specific or dock/system-related.

CCR.Complaint: Console displays error code 03 during self-test, tool will not start.
CCR.Cause: Batteries confirmed charged; power cycle did not clear error; likely internal console fault.
CCR.Resolution: Console removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent to CE bench for repair.
