If reseating or replacing a connector restores suction, document the connection issue and stop.

steps.title: Check the Fluid Collection Level and Tank Status
steps.instructions: Action: Verify the rover is not full, near full, or reporting a tank level issue. Confirm the fluid level display makes sense compared with actual use. Expected outcome: The tank has available capacity and the level sensing appears reasonable. Why it matters: A full or incorrectly sensed tank may cause suction to reduce, stop, or alarm. If the tank is full, have the rover exchanged, emptied through the proper docking process, or handled per facility procedure. Stop troubleshooting once suction is restored.

steps.title: Inspect the Filter Status
steps.instructions: Action: Check for any filter warning, airflow restriction message, or visibly saturated/incorrectly installed filter. Expected outcome: Filters are installed correctly, dry where applicable, and not blocked. Why it matters: Restricted airflow can reduce suction strength or cause suction to drop during use. If filter replacement or proper installation restores suction, document the filter condition and stop.

steps.title: Check for Liquid or Debris in the Wrong Area
steps.instructions: Action: Look for signs of fluid spillover, residue, or contamination around external connection points, inlet areas, tubing ports, or filters. Expected outcome: External ports and accessible connection areas are clean, dry, and unobstructed. Why it matters: Fluid or debris in the suction pathway can restrict flow and may indicate improper setup, overfill, or contamination. If fluid intrusion is suspected beyond normal external cleaning, remove the device from service for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Test With Known-Good Tubing and Accessory
steps.instructions: Action: Remove the current clinical tubing/accessory setup and test suction using known-good tubing and an appropriate test setup. Expected outcome: Suction performance improves if the original tubing or accessory was the problem. Why it matters: This separates a Neptune issue from a disposable or setup issue. If suction is normal with known-good tubing, return the device only after confirming the clinical setup problem has been corrected.

steps.title: Check Whether the Issue Is Port-Specific
steps.instructions: Action: If the Neptune has multiple suction connections available, compare suction behavior between available ports using the same known-good tubing setup. Expected outcome: All active ports should behave consistently. Why it matters: One weak port may indicate a local obstruction, damaged connector, or port-specific issue. Weak suction on all ports points toward a broader system issue. If one port remains weak or nonfunctional, remove the device from service for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Check for Docking or Waste Transfer-Related Conditions
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the rover was properly docked, drained, and prepared for use before the case. Check for any recent docking, drain, or waste transfer issue reported by staff. Expected outcome: The rover is ready for use and not carrying over a prior waste transfer problem. Why it matters: If the system was not properly emptied or reset after docking, suction performance may be affected during the next use. If docking or waste transfer failure is suspected, remove the rover from service until the docking issue is corrected.

steps.title: Listen for Abnormal Operating Sounds
steps.instructions: Action: During a safe test, listen for unusual motor noise, pulsing, rattling, excessive strain, or no motor activity when suction is requested. Expected outcome: The unit sounds consistent and responds normally when suction is activated. Why it matters: Abnormal noise or no vacuum response after external causes are ruled out may indicate internal vacuum, motor, valve, sensor, or control failure. If abnormal internal operation is suspected, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

steps.title: Perform a Final Functional Check
steps.instructions: Action: After any correction, verify suction using a safe test setup before returning the unit to clinical use. Expected outcome: Suction is stable, alarms are clear, tubing connections remain secure, and the unit performs as expected. Why it matters: A temporary improvement is not enough. The device must demonstrate stable suction before returning to service. If suction is restored and stable, document the corrective action and return the unit per facility process.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the Stryker Neptune 3 had weak suction and suction dropped during fluid collection.
CCR.Cause: Found suction tubing partially kinked behind the rover and one tubing connection not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Rerouted tubing, secured the connection, verified stable suction with known-good tubing, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the issue was weak suction, no suction, or suction dropping during use
Whether the problem affected one port or all suction ports
Docking or waste transfer history reviewed
Any unusual sounds from the unit
Signs of fluid, debris, heat, smell, or contamination

title: Stryker Neptune 3 Surgical Fluid Management System - Rover Docking, Docking Station, Or Waste Transfer Failure
description: Troubleshooting Neptune 3 rover docking, docking station alignment, drain connection, waste transfer, and external setup problems.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the Neptune 3 is not being used on an active patient or during an active surgical case before troubleshooting docking or waste transfer problems. Expected outcome: The device is removed from clinical use before service checks begin. Why it matters: Waste transfer and docking issues can interrupt suction availability, create fluid exposure risk, or cause contamination concerns. If this resolves the immediate clinical need by moving the case to another suction source, stop and document the action.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Docking or Transfer Problem
steps.instructions: Action: Ask staff what was observed. Confirm whether the issue is: Rover will not dock; Rover will not recognize the docking station; Waste transfer will not start; Waste transfer starts then stops; Drain or transfer fault appears; Docking station does not power or respond; Rover does not empty after docking. Expected outcome: The exact symptom is confirmed before troubleshooting. Why it matters: “Will not dock” may be a mechanical alignment problem, while “will not transfer” may involve drain connection, tank level sensing, power, or dock communication.

steps.title: Inspect the Docking Area for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Action: Check the floor area, docking station, and rover path for carts, debris, raised floor transitions, cables, fluid, or anything preventing proper alignment. Expected outcome: The rover can approach the docking station straight and fully seat into position. Why it matters: A rover that is slightly misaligned may appear docked but fail to make the required mechanical or communication connection. If obstruction removal restores docking and transfer operation, stop and document.

steps.title: Check Docking Station Power
steps.instructions: Action: Verify the docking station is plugged into a known-good outlet. Check for power indicators, tripped GFCI, loose plugs, damaged cords, or switched outlets. Expected outcome: The docking station has stable facility power and normal indicator status. Why it matters: If the dock is not powered, the rover may physically dock but fail to recognize the station or begin waste transfer. If restoring power resolves the issue, stop and document.

steps.title: Inspect the Rover Exterior and Docking Contacts
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect the rear docking interface on the rover and the mating area on the docking station. Look for visible damage, bent guides, cracked plastic, contamination, dried waste residue, or foreign material. Expected outcome: The docking surfaces are clean, intact, and able to mate properly. Why it matters: Waste residue or physical damage can prevent the rover from fully seating or communicating with the dock. If cleaning visible external contamination restores normal docking, stop and document.

steps.title: Confirm the Rover Is Fully Seated
steps.instructions: Action: Reposition the rover and dock it again using normal staff-facing operation. Do not force it. Confirm it locks or settles into the expected docked position. Expected outcome: The rover seats evenly and the system recognizes the docked condition. Why it matters: A partially docked rover can cause transfer failure even if it looks close enough visually. If proper alignment resolves the issue, stop and document.

steps.title: Check the Waste Transfer Path
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect external waste transfer hoses, drain tubing, dock drain connection, and visible plumbing connections for kinks, blockage, loose fittings, or improper routing. Expected outcome: The waste transfer path is connected, open, and not visibly restricted. Why it matters: A blocked or kinked waste path can prevent the rover from emptying or cause the transfer cycle to stop. If correcting the hose or drain routing resolves the issue, stop and document.

steps.title: Check for Drain or Facility Plumbing Problems
steps.instructions: Action: Determine whether other docked rovers or waste systems are having the same problem at the same docking location. If available, test the rover at another known-good docking station. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to either the rover, the docking station, or the facility drain connection. Why it matters: A clogged or restricted facility drain can look like a Neptune 3 failure when the device itself is functioning normally. If the rover works at another dock, remove the original dock from service and notify facilities or appropriate support.

steps.title: Check for Tank Full or Level-Related Conditions
steps.instructions: Action: Review the rover display or indicators for tank full, waste level, drain, or transfer-related messages. Expected outcome: The displayed condition matches the actual state of the rover and transfer process. Why it matters: A tank level or drain-related fault may prevent waste transfer or make the rover appear unable to empty. If the issue is a simple full-tank or incomplete-transfer condition and a successful transfer clears it, stop and document.

steps.title: Power Cycle Only When Safe
steps.instructions: Action: If allowed by department procedure and the rover is not in patient use, power cycle the rover and retry docking. Expected outcome: The rover boots normally, recognizes the dock, and begins the expected transfer sequence. Why it matters: Temporary communication or software lockup conditions may clear after a controlled restart. If the issue clears after restart and the unit passes functional checks, document and return to service only if performance is normal.

steps.title: Compare with a Known-Good Rover or Dock
steps.instructions: Action: If possible, dock a known-good rover at the suspected docking station, or dock the suspect rover at a known-good station. Expected outcome: The failure follows either the rover or the docking station. Why it matters: This prevents unnecessary repair of the wrong component. If the problem follows the rover, remove the rover from service. If the problem stays with the dock, remove the docking station from service.

steps.title: Inspect for Leaks, Odor, Unusual Noise, or Heat
steps.instructions: Action: During safe testing, observe for fluid leaks, abnormal pump noise, unusual vibration, burning smell, overheating, or repeated transfer aborts. Expected outcome: No abnormal physical condition is present. Why it matters: Waste transfer involves fluid movement and powered components. Leaks, odor, heat, or abnormal sounds suggest the unit should not remain in service. If any unsafe condition is found, stop troubleshooting and remove the device from service.

steps.title: Perform a Final Functional Check
steps.instructions: Action: After any correction, verify the rover docks properly, the dock is recognized, waste transfer starts, transfer completes, and no new alarms or faults appear. Expected outcome: Docking and waste transfer operate normally from start to finish. Why it matters: Clearing the initial symptom is not enough. The system must complete the full transfer process safely before return to service.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the Stryker Neptune 3 rover would dock but would not begin waste transfer at the docking station.
CCR.Cause: Found the rover was not fully seating due to debris and dried residue on the external docking interface.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the external docking interface, confirmed proper docking alignment, completed a successful waste transfer cycle, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Rover display message or fault shown
Whether the dock recognized the rover
Whether waste transfer started or stopped
Hose, drain, or transfer path condition
Any leak, odor, noise, heat, or residue found
Whether another rover worked at the same dock
Whether the suspect rover worked at another dock

title: Stryker Neptune 3 Surgical Fluid Management System - Fluid Level, Tank Full, Drain, or Waste Canister Sensing Issue
description: Troubleshooting tank full, fluid level, drain, or waste sensing issues caused by setup, canister, connection, drain, or sensor-related problems.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the Neptune 3 is not actively supporting a procedure before troubleshooting. If the issue occurs during a case, have clinical staff switch to an alternate suction or waste collection method first. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on a system with unresolved waste handling or suction interruption. Why it matters: Fluid management problems can interrupt suction, cause overflow risk, or delay the procedure. If this resolves the immediate clinical need, stop and evaluate the device after the case.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the exact complaint or message being reported. Identify whether the issue is related to: Tank full indication; Fluid level not reading correctly; Drain not starting; Drain not completing; Waste canister or manifold sensing issue; Repeated alarms after emptying. Expected outcome: The failure mode is clearly identified before parts or sensors are suspected. Why it matters: “Tank full,” “will not drain,” and “not sensing canister” may have different causes.

steps.title: Check the Tank or Waste Container Status
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect the collection tank or waste container status. Confirm whether the tank is actually full, partially full, empty, or recently drained. Expected outcome: The displayed status should match the physical condition of the waste container. Why it matters: A true full condition is not a device failure. If the tank is full, follow the approved clinical waste disposal process and retest. If the tank was full and the alarm clears after proper emptying, stop.

steps.title: Inspect for Improper Setup or Incorrect Accessories
steps.instructions: Action: Verify that the correct Stryker-approved waste collection setup, manifold, tubing, and accessories are installed correctly. Expected outcome: All accessories are seated, aligned, and compatible with the Neptune 3 system. Why it matters: Incorrect or poorly seated accessories can prevent the system from sensing the waste path correctly. If reseating or correcting the accessory setup resolves the issue, document and stop.

steps.title: Check for Kinked, Blocked, or Pinched Tubing
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect all visible suction and drain tubing for kinks, clogs, pinches, collapsed sections, or fluid blockage. Expected outcome: Tubing should be open, routed correctly, and free of visible obstruction. Why it matters: A blocked fluid path can mimic a full tank, poor drain, or failed waste flow condition. If tubing correction restores normal operation, stop.

steps.title: Confirm the Drain Connection and Drain Destination
steps.instructions: Action: Verify that the drain hose or docking/drain connection is fully seated and routed to the correct approved drain location. Expected outcome: The device should recognize the drain connection and allow draining when commanded. Why it matters: A loose drain connection or improper drain setup may prevent the system from entering or completing drain mode. If correcting the drain connection resolves the problem, stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Waste Canister or Tank Seating
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the waste container, tank, lid, seals, or related removable components are fully seated and latched as intended. Expected outcome: The system should detect the waste container/tank and operate without false sensing errors. Why it matters: Slight misalignment can cause a sensing issue even when the tank appears installed. If reseating the component clears the message, stop.

steps.title: Check for Fluid, Debris, or Residue Around Sensing Areas
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect externally accessible sensing areas, tank interface points, drain ports, and connection points for dried fluid, debris, residue, or contamination. Expected outcome: Sensing and connection areas should be clean, dry, and unobstructed. Why it matters: Fluid residue or debris can interfere with level detection, accessory recognition, or drain sensing. If cleaning accessible external areas resolves the issue, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device Safely
steps.instructions: Action: Once the device is disconnected from patient use and fluid handling is safe, power the Neptune 3 off, wait briefly, and power it back on. Expected outcome: The system should restart normally and recheck tank, drain, and accessory status. Why it matters: Some sensing faults may be temporary logic or communication issues. If the device restarts and passes normal checks without alarms, perform a functional check and return to service if appropriate.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good Compatible Setup
steps.instructions: Action: If available, test using a known-good compatible manifold, tubing set, drain connection, or waste setup. Expected outcome: The problem should either follow the accessory setup or remain with the device. Why it matters: Swapping external accessories helps separate a disposable/setup issue from a device sensing issue. If the issue follows the accessory, replace the accessory and stop.

steps.title: Check for Repeated False Full or False Empty Indications
steps.instructions: Action: Observe whether the device repeatedly reports full when empty, empty when fluid is present, or fails to recognize a drain cycle after setup has been verified. Expected outcome: Fluid level and tank status should reasonably match the actual condition. Why it matters: Repeated false indications after setup checks may indicate a sensor, internal connection, calibration, or control issue.

steps.title: Perform a Final Operational Check
steps.instructions: Action: After any correction, verify that the Neptune 3 powers up normally, recognizes the waste setup, does not falsely alarm, and can complete the expected drain or fluid handling process. Expected outcome: The device operates normally without repeated tank full, drain, or waste sensing messages. Why it matters: A single cleared alarm is not enough if the device immediately fails again during normal operation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Stryker Neptune 3 was indicating tank full and would not allow normal fluid collection.
CCR.Cause: Verified the tank was not full, reseated the waste setup, inspected the drain connection, and found the drain hose not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the drain connection, power cycled the unit, confirmed the tank full message cleared, and verified normal drain and waste sensing operation.

helpfulDetails: Whether the tank was actually full
Tubing checked for kinks or blockage
Any visible debris, residue, or fluid near sensing areas
Whether a known-good accessory setup was tested
Whether the issue followed the accessory or stayed with the unit
Indicator lights, alarm behavior, or touchscreen messages
Power behavior during restart or drain attempt
Environmental factors such as waste handling area, docking location, or spill exposure
Final device status: returned to service or removed from service

title: Stryker Neptune 3 Surgical Fluid Management System - Smoke Evacuation, Filter, Or Airflow Fault
description: Troubleshooting smoke evacuation airflow, filter, tubing, suction setup, or blockage issues on the Stryker Neptune 3.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Action: If the Neptune 3 is being used during a procedure and smoke evacuation is not working properly, notify OR staff immediately and provide alternate smoke evacuation or suction support. Expected outcome: Surgical smoke is controlled using a safe alternate method before troubleshooting continues. Why it matters: Smoke evacuation issues can expose staff and patients to surgical plume and may affect visibility at the surgical site.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Problem
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the exact issue reported by staff. Ask whether the problem is: Weak smoke evacuation; No airflow; Filter warning; Filter missing or not recognized; Airflow fault; Unusual noise from the smoke evacuation system; Tubing collapse or blockage. Expected outcome: The complaint is confirmed and separated from general suction or fluid collection issues. Why it matters: Smoke evacuation, suction, and fluid management problems can sound similar but may involve different accessories and flow paths.

steps.title: Check That the Correct Smoke Evacuation Setup Is Being Used
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the Neptune 3 is set up with the proper smoke evacuation tubing, filter, wand, pencil adapter, or suction accessory required for the procedure. Expected outcome: The system is connected with compatible smoke evacuation accessories. If the wrong accessory or setup is found, correct the setup, test airflow, and stop if the issue is resolved.

steps.title: Inspect the Smoke Evacuation Filter
steps.instructions: Action: Check that the filter is installed correctly, fully seated, and not expired, saturated, damaged, or visibly contaminated. Expected outcome: The filter is present, secure, and appropriate for use. Why it matters: A missing, full, blocked, or poorly seated filter can reduce airflow or trigger a filter-related fault. If replacing or reseating the filter clears the fault, document the filter issue and return the unit to service after functional verification.

steps.title: Check for Tubing Kinks, Blockages, or Collapsed Lines
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect the smoke evacuation tubing from the patient end back to the Neptune 3. Look for: Kinked tubing; Crushed tubing; Fluid inside the smoke evacuation line; Debris or tissue blockage; Loose tubing connections; Tubing connected to the wrong port. Expected outcome: Tubing is open, dry, properly routed, and connected to the correct smoke evacuation path. If tubing replacement restores airflow, stop troubleshooting and document the accessory failure.

steps.title: Check the Patient-End Accessory
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect the smoke evacuation pencil, wand, nozzle, or laparoscopic tubing connection for obstruction or improper assembly. Expected outcome: The patient-end accessory allows unrestricted airflow. Why it matters: A clogged wand or pencil adapter can make the Neptune appear faulty even when the base unit is working normally.

steps.title: Verify Smoke Evacuation Settings
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the smoke evacuation function is turned on and set to the expected level for the procedure. Check whether staff are using automatic activation, manual activation, or footswitch/remote activation if applicable. Expected outcome: The smoke evacuation mode and flow setting match clinical use. If the unit was set too low or not activated, adjust settings, verify airflow, and stop if resolved.

steps.title: Check for Alarm or Indicator Behavior
steps.instructions: Action: Observe the screen or indicators for filter warnings, airflow restriction messages, or smoke evacuation fault messages. Expected outcome: The displayed message matches the reported issue. Why it matters: A filter warning points toward filter seating, filter life, or obstruction. An airflow fault may point toward blocked tubing, filter restriction, or internal blower/sensor failure.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Unit When Safe
steps.instructions: Action: When the unit is not connected to active patient use, power it down, wait briefly, and power it back up. Expected outcome: Temporary software or detection issues clear, and the smoke evacuation system initializes normally. If the fault clears, perform a basic operational check before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Test With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Action: Replace the smoke evacuation filter, tubing, and patient-end accessory with known-good compatible items. Expected outcome: Airflow improves and the fault clears if the issue was caused by an accessory or consumable. Why it matters: Smoke evacuation faults are commonly caused by external disposables before the base unit is actually defective.

steps.title: Check for Unusual Sounds, Heat, or Smell
steps.instructions: Action: Listen for abnormal blower noise, grinding, rattling, or a fan that does not appear to run. Check for unusual heat or burning smell near the smoke evacuation section. Expected outcome: The unit operates without abnormal noise, odor, or overheating. If abnormal blower behavior, heat, or odor is present, remove the device from service.

steps.title: Perform a Basic Functional Airflow Check
steps.instructions: Action: With proper accessories installed, activate smoke evacuation and verify that airflow is present at the patient-end accessory. Expected outcome: Airflow is strong and consistent, with no active filter or airflow fault. If airflow is still weak or absent after filter, tubing, accessory, and setting checks, escalate for repair.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the Stryker Neptune 3 had a smoke evacuation airflow fault and weak smoke capture during setup.
CCR.Cause: Found smoke evacuation filter not fully seated and smoke tubing partially kinked near the connection port.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the smoke evacuation filter, replaced kinked tubing, verified airflow at the smoke evacuation accessory, and returned unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Smoke evacuation filter checked or replaced
Filter warning or airflow message observed
Tubing checked for kinks, fluid, or blockage
Smoke pencil, wand, or adapter inspected
Unusual blower noise, heat, or smell noted
Final device status: returned to service or removed from service

title: Stryker Neptune 3 Surgical Fluid Management System - Touchscreen, Battery, Power-Up, Or Communication Failure
description: Troubleshooting Neptune 3 touchscreen response, battery charging, power-up, docking, or communication-related failures before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the Neptune 3 is not actively supporting a surgical procedure before troubleshooting. If the issue occurs during a case, have clinical staff transition to an approved backup suction or fluid management method. Expected outcome: Patient care and surgical workflow are maintained using safe alternate equipment. Why it matters: Loss of suction, power, screen control, or communication during a procedure can affect fluid removal and case safety.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Problem
steps.instructions: Action: Ask staff exactly what failed and when it happened. Confirm whether the issue is: Touchscreen not responding; Unit will not power on; Battery will not charge or has short runtime; Unit powers up but freezes; Docking or rover communication issue; Error appears during startup or connection. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified before parts or internal faults are assumed. Why it matters: Touchscreen, battery, power, and communication complaints can look similar but have different causes.

steps.title: Check AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Action: Confirm the power cord is plugged into a working hospital-grade outlet. Test the outlet or move the unit to a known-good outlet. Expected outcome: The unit powers on or begins charging normally. If resolved: Document the bad outlet or power source issue and stop troubleshooting. Why it matters: A dead outlet or switched circuit can mimic battery, power supply, or charging failure.

steps.title: Inspect the Power Cord and Plug
steps.instructions: Action: Check the power cord for cuts, crushed insulation, loose plug blades, bent contacts, strain relief damage, or signs of overheating. Expected outcome: Cord is intact, secure, and safe to use. If damaged: Remove the device from service until the cord issue is corrected. Why it matters: Damaged power cords create both power reliability and electrical safety concerns.

steps.title: Confirm Proper Power-Up Sequence
steps.instructions: Action: Turn the unit off, disconnect from AC power if safe to do so, wait at least 30 seconds, reconnect power, and attempt normal startup. Expected outcome: The Neptune 3 completes startup without freezing or faulting. If resolved: Perform a functional check and document that a power reset restored operation. Why it matters: Temporary software lockups or incomplete shutdowns may cause startup or touchscreen issues.

steps.title: Check Battery Charge Status
steps.instructions: Action: Connect the unit to AC power and allow it to charge. Observe battery indicators, charging messages, or power status lights. Expected outcome: The battery indicates charging and the unit remains powered on. If the unit only works on AC power: Suspect weak battery capacity, failed battery charging circuit, or battery connection issue requiring bench evaluation. Why it matters: Low or failed batteries can cause power-up failures, unexpected shutdowns, or communication interruptions.

steps.title: Inspect for Battery-Related Symptoms
steps.instructions: Action: Ask whether the unit shuts down quickly after being unplugged, fails during transport, or reports low battery soon after charging. Expected outcome: Battery runtime is reasonable and consistent. If battery runtime is poor: Remove from service for battery evaluation or replacement per facility procedure. Why it matters: A weak battery may pass initial power-up but fail during movement or use.

steps.title: Check Touchscreen Surface and Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect the touchscreen for fluid residue, disinfectant buildup, cracks, delamination, pressure damage, or foreign material. Clean the screen using facility-approved methods and retest. Expected outcome: Touchscreen responds accurately to touch inputs. If resolved: Return to service after confirming normal screen function. Why it matters: Residue, fluid exposure, or damaged screen surfaces can cause poor touch response or false touches.

steps.title: Confirm the Unit Is Not Frozen
steps.instructions: Action: Observe whether the display is active but buttons do not respond, the screen is stuck during startup, or the same message remains displayed. Expected outcome: The user interface responds after a normal restart. If still frozen: Remove the device from service for software, display, or controller evaluation. Why it matters: A frozen display may indicate software lockup, touchscreen failure, or internal control communication failure.

steps.title: Inspect Docking and Communication Connections
steps.instructions: Action: If the issue involves docking, rover connection, canister recognition, or communication between Neptune components, inspect visible docking contacts and connection points for debris, fluid, bent pins, or poor seating. Expected outcome: The device docks fully and recognizes connected components. If resolved: Clean or reseat as appropriate, then perform functional checks. Why it matters: Poor physical connection can appear as a communication fault even when electronics are functional.

steps.title: Verify Accessories and Connected Components
steps.instructions: Action: Remove and reconnect compatible accessories, rover components, manifolds, or collection components involved in the reported issue. Use known-good accessories when available. Expected outcome: The system recognizes accessories and communicates normally. If a swapped accessory resolves the issue: Replace or remove the faulty accessory from use. Why it matters: Accessory faults can cause system errors that look like a main unit communication failure.

steps.title: Check for Visible Fluid Intrusion or Contamination
steps.instructions: Action: Inspect external surfaces, docking areas, vents, screen edges, and connection points for fluid, residue, corrosion, unusual odor, or signs of exposure. Expected outcome: No evidence of fluid intrusion or contamination is present. If fluid intrusion is suspected: Remove from service and send for evaluation. Why it matters: Surgical fluid systems operate around liquids, and fluid exposure can affect power, communication, touchscreen function, and safety.

steps.title: Listen and Observe During Startup
steps.instructions: Action: During power-up, observe indicator lights, display behavior, fan or motor sounds, relay clicks, alarms, or unusual noises. Expected outcome: Startup behavior is consistent and completes normally. If abnormal sounds, heat, smell, or repeated faults occur: Stop troubleshooting and remove from service. Why it matters: Startup behavior helps separate external power issues from internal electronics or power supply problems.

steps.title: Perform a Basic Functional Check
steps.instructions: Action: If the issue appears corrected, verify the unit powers on, touchscreen responds, battery charges, communication/docking functions normally, and no active errors remain. Expected outcome: The Neptune 3 operates normally and is safe to return to service. If all checks pass: Document findings and return the unit to service.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Stryker Neptune 3 would power on but the touchscreen was frozen and would not respond during setup.
CCR.Cause: Verified AC power was good, power cord was intact, and the touchscreen remained unresponsive after restart and screen cleaning.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the Neptune 3 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for bench evaluation of the touchscreen/control interface.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested or unit moved to known-good outlet
Whether unit works on AC only
Any visible fluid residue or contamination

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: N/C Battery Low
description: Troubleshooting the N/C Battery Low message indicating inadequate nurse call battery voltage and potentially unreliable nurse call signaling.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from nurse-call-dependent clinical use until corrected. Provide an alternate verified nurse call method or transfer the patient to a bed with confirmed Nurse Call operation before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Associated Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the display shows N/C Battery Low and verify the bed is equipped with the Nurse Call option. Document whether the message occurs at startup, remains displayed, occurs intermittently, or is associated with unreliable Nurse Call behavior.

steps.title: Confirm Bed Power and Basic Operating Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the bed is connected to a known-good AC outlet and otherwise powers and operates normally. Inspect the power cord, plug, and visible connections for damage, looseness, contamination, or overheating.

steps.title: Inspect the Nurse Call Interface and External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the nurse call cable, plug, receptacle, and accessible connection points for looseness, damaged pins, frayed or pinched cable sections, contamination, or broken housings. Reseat accessible connections as appropriate.

steps.title: Inspect the Nurse Call Battery Condition and Connection
steps.instructions: With the bed removed from patient use, inspect the nurse call battery and accessible connections for looseness, damaged wiring, corrosion, contamination, swelling, leakage, or incorrect installation. The message indicates battery voltage below the required 5 V threshold.

steps.title: Replace the Low Nurse Call Battery as Indicated
steps.instructions: Replace a low, damaged, aged, disconnected, or unreliable battery with the correct approved Nurse Call battery. Ensure the replacement is fully seated and safely routed.

steps.title: Verify Nurse Call Operation After Correction
steps.instructions: Confirm the N/C Battery Low message is cleared, connect the bed to an approved Nurse Call test setup or clinical interface, activate Nurse Call, and verify the call is received and annunciated correctly.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If correcting the battery connection or replacing the battery clears the message and Nurse Call passes functional testing, document the repair and return the bed to service according to department procedure.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed N/C Battery Low. Nurse Call function considered unreliable pending evaluation because the displayed message indicates low nurse call battery voltage.
CCR.Cause: Nurse call battery found below acceptable operating condition and unable to maintain required voltage, resulting in the N/C Battery Low message. External nurse call cable and accessible connections inspected with no additional damage noted.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from nurse-call-dependent use, replaced nurse call battery, secured associated connections, confirmed message cleared, and verified Nurse Call activation operated normally before returning bed to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: Fowler Calib. Err
description: Troubleshooting Fowler Calib. Err, indicating incomplete Fowler calibration that may prevent reliable head-section position indication or related bed operation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use if Fowler position cannot be trusted or does not move normally. Transfer the patient to a known-working bed before troubleshooting when clinically necessary. Never troubleshoot while an active patient depends on Fowler positioning.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that Fowler Calib. Err appears in the lower status screen during normal mode. Operate the Fowler/head-section function through a limited safe range and document whether movement is normal, limited, intermittent, noisy, or accompanied by additional errors.

steps.title: Check Power and Basic Bed Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm appropriate AC power and normal power-related indicators. Inspect for visible damage, contamination, fluid intrusion, or external obstruction from linens, mattress components, accessories, cables, or attached equipment.

steps.title: Inspect the Fowler Position-Sensing Path
steps.instructions: Visually inspect accessible portions of the Fowler potentiometer area, linkage, wiring, and connectors for loose connections, damaged wiring, mechanical disengagement, contamination, or abnormal movement. Do not perform unnecessary internal disassembly during initial evaluation.

steps.title: Verify Fowler Movement Before Calibration
steps.instructions: Verify that the Fowler/head section moves smoothly without binding, unexpected stopping, unusual noise, or erratic operation. Stop testing if movement becomes unpredictable or unsafe.

steps.title: Complete the Fowler Calibration Procedure
steps.instructions: Perform the applicable Fowler calibration procedure according to approved service documentation for the Stryker S3. Return the bed to normal operating mode and confirm whether Fowler Calib. Err clears.

steps.title: Verify Normal Operation After Calibration
steps.instructions: Function-test Fowler movement through its intended operating range. Confirm smooth and repeatable operation, no recurrence of Fowler Calib. Err, and no additional bed errors before returning the bed to service according to facility procedure.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Fowler Calib. Err in the lower status screen during normal mode, indicating Fowler calibration had not been completed.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the Fowler position-sensing path required evaluation for calibration completion. Accessible Fowler potentiometer wiring and linkage were inspected for loose connections, damage, or mechanical disengagement.
CCR.Resolution: Verified Fowler movement was unobstructed, completed Fowler calibration per approved service procedure, confirmed the message cleared, and function-tested Fowler operation without recurrence. Bed returned to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: Scale Calib. Err
description: Troubleshooting Scale Calib. Err when the installed scale is unavailable or unreliable because scale calibration has not been completed.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use for care that depends on accurate weight, Bed Exit, or related scale-based monitoring. Move the patient to a known-good bed or use an approved alternate weighing method before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Bed Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that Scale Calib. Err is displayed in the lower status screen during normal operating mode, verify that the bed has an installed scale system, and check for additional scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness errors.

steps.title: Check Power, Bed Condition, and External Interference
steps.instructions: Confirm known-good power, inspect visible cords and cables, and remove external contact from objects, linens, hoses, cables, accessories, or unstable positioning that could influence the weighing structure.

steps.title: Confirm the Bed Is Prepared for Scale Calibration
steps.instructions: Remove the patient, prepare the mattress and intended accessories according to facility practice and applicable service information, and have the specified calibration weight available.

steps.title: Perform the Scale Calibration Procedure
steps.instructions: Enter the Maintenance Menu, select Calib. Scale, and follow displayed prompts exactly, including Do Not Touch Bed, Place Weight in Center, Trendelenburg, and reverse Trendelenburg steps as prompted.

steps.title: Verify Scale Performance After Calibration
steps.instructions: Confirm the message clears, verify stable and accurate scale performance with a known test weight or approved functional method, and check that no related scale-based system errors remain.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the bed to service only when calibration completes successfully, the Scale Calib. Err message is cleared, and scale performance is verified as accurate.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Scale Calib. Err in normal operating mode. Installed scale system was not available for reliable patient weighing until calibration was completed.
CCR.Cause: Scale system calibration had not been completed. Bed was inspected for external interference and prepared for calibration with no abnormal contact or instability identified.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from patient use, entered the Maintenance Menu, selected Calib. Scale, and completed the displayed calibration sequence using the required centered test weight and prompted bed-position steps. Verified stable scale performance with a known weight and confirmed the Scale Calib. Err message cleared. Bed returned to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: Function Disabled
description: Troubleshooting Function Disabled - Call Service when Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness operation is blocked by an active logged fault and cannot be trusted for clinical monitoring.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not rely on the affected Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness function while this message is active. If the bed is occupied and the disabled function is required for patient safety, provide alternate monitoring or fall-prevention measures and move the patient to an appropriate backup arrangement before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the bed removed from patient-dependent use as appropriate, observe whether Function Disabled - Call Service appears when attempting to activate Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness. Document which function request causes the message.

steps.title: Check Basic External Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm stable AC power. Inspect accessible cables, connectors, siderails, footboard connections, and control interfaces for damage, looseness, pinching, contamination, or fluid intrusion. Check for frame, accessory, cord, linen, or environmental interference.

steps.title: Identify Which Function Is Disabled
steps.instructions: Determine whether Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness is unavailable. Do not assume the disabled function itself has failed because operation may be blocked by another logged fault affecting safe use.

steps.title: Review the Error Log
steps.instructions: Use the appropriate Maintenance Menu function to review the Error Log for the underlying condition. Possible associated system messages include 901 ScaleSystem, 902 BedExitSystem, and 903 LBSSystem. Look for more specific load-cell, zeroing, communication, or siderail-switch faults.

steps.title: Isolate External or Accessory-Related Causes
steps.instructions: Based on the underlying logged fault, inspect accessible external conditions such as frame interference, unstable positioning, damaged visible wiring, loose connections, siderail lock action, or switch actuation areas. Correct only confirmed external issues.

steps.title: Verify the Corrected Function
steps.instructions: After the source fault has been addressed according to service procedure, verify that the previously disabled function activates and performs correctly and that Function Disabled - Call Service no longer appears.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the message is resolved and the affected function passes operational verification, document the work and return the bed to service according to department procedure. If unresolved, remove the bed from service for repair evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 displayed Function Disabled - Call Service when attempting to activate Bed Exit. Bed Exit function could not be enabled for clinical use.
CCR.Cause: Reviewed Error Log and identified an active logged system fault affecting the Bed Exit function. External inspection completed; no accessory interference or visible connection issue corrected the condition. Underlying device fault remains suspected.
CCR.Resolution: Confirmed Bed Exit could not be relied upon, notified clinical staff to use alternate patient-safety measures, removed bed from service, labeled unit Out of Service, and referred for further repair evaluation.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: Turn off Bed Exit
description: Troubleshooting Turn off Bed Exit - Call Service when an underlying scale or Bed Exit system fault makes patient fall-risk monitoring unreliable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Treat Bed Exit monitoring as unreliable while the message or associated alarm condition is present. If the bed is occupied, coordinate alternate fall-prevention or patient-monitoring measures before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the display shows Turn off Bed Exit - Call Service, whether Bed Exit is armed, and whether the Bed Exit alarm is sounding or masking the service message. Note any abnormal Scale or iBED Awareness behavior.

steps.title: Safely Disarm Bed Exit for Service Evaluation
steps.instructions: After alternate patient-safety measures are in place, disarm Bed Exit as appropriate for service evaluation. Do not dismiss the message and return the bed to use without correcting and verifying the underlying fault.

steps.title: Check Power, Connections, and External Condition
steps.instructions: Verify normal power, inspect visible cords and accessible external connections, check for fluid intrusion or impact damage, and ensure no accessories, tubing, linens, cords, or nearby objects interfere with the bed frame or weighing structure.

steps.title: Verify Scale and Bed Position Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm the bed is stable on the floor and free of anything contacting, pulling on, or binding against its frame, siderails, casters, or weighing structure. Check for unstable, incorrect, or unavailable scale readings.

steps.title: Review the Error Log for the Underlying 200-Level Fault
steps.instructions: Access service or maintenance error-log information and identify the associated 200-level error, including load-cell, scale communication, ADC-related, zeroing, or unstable-zero faults. Document the specific code found.

steps.title: Isolate External Versus Device-Related Causes
steps.instructions: Inspect the affected accessible area based on the logged fault. Check for visible load-cell interference, cable damage, pinched wiring, loose accessible connections, unstable bed position, or other external causes without internal disassembly.

steps.title: Correct Identified External Issues and Recheck Operation
steps.instructions: Correct identified external causes according to department procedure, recheck the displayed message and error log, verify scale operation, and test Bed Exit only after the scale-related fault is cleared.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: When the underlying fault is corrected and Bed Exit operation verifies normally, document the repair and return the bed to service according to department policy.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Turn off Bed Exit - Call Service while Bed Exit was armed. Bed Exit monitoring was considered unreliable, and associated alarm behavior was evaluated.
CCR.Cause: Error log identified an underlying 200-level scale or Bed Exit fault affecting reliable Bed Exit operation. External interference, bed stability, and visible connection conditions were inspected; the fault remained present.
CCR.Resolution: Bed Exit was removed from clinical reliance, alternate patient-safety measures were communicated as applicable, and the bed was labeled Out of Service for repair evaluation of the underlying scale or Bed Exit fault.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: Turn off Awareness
description: Troubleshooting Turn off Awareness - Call Service when iBED Awareness is unreliable due to an underlying scale, load-cell, communication, zeroing, or siderail-switch fault.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not rely on iBED Awareness indicators or monitoring while this message is active. If the bed is occupied or in clinical use, notify clinical staff and provide alternate fall-prevention and patient-monitoring measures according to facility policy before troubleshooting. Turn off iBED Awareness for service evaluation only after patient safety has been addressed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display shows Turn off Awareness - Call Service. Determine whether the message occurs during startup, when iBED Awareness is turned on, after siderail movement, during scale or Bed Exit operation, or intermittently during use. Note associated scale, Bed Exit, siderail-status, or additional service error behavior.

steps.title: Check Power and Basic Bed Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm connection to a known-good power source and inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, and visible connections. Inspect for contamination, fluid intrusion, impact damage, pinched cables, or external interference around the bed frame, siderails, and weighing structure.

steps.title: Confirm Siderail Position and Mechanical Operation
steps.instructions: Manually inspect each siderail for proper movement and locking. Observe whether iBED Awareness correctly recognizes position changes. Inspect visible siderail switch areas, cable routing, and accessible connectors for damage, disconnection, contamination, misalignment, or incomplete latching.

steps.title: Check for Scale or Load-Cell-Related Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that nothing is contacting, loading, or interfering with the bed frame or weighing structure. Inspect for trapped items, cable or linen interference, unstable caster position, wall contact, or visible damage near load-cell areas. Observe whether scale operation or zeroing produces additional errors when appropriate for service evaluation.

steps.title: Review the Error Log
steps.instructions: Access the approved service or maintenance error log and identify the underlying fault. Look for 200-level scale, load-cell, zeroing, or communication errors and 300-level siderail-switch errors. Document the specific code and affected subsystem.

steps.title: Isolate the Affected Subsystem
steps.instructions: Use the logged error to focus external inspection on the indicated siderail switch, load-cell area, zeroing condition, or accessible communication harness and connectors. Do not perform internal board-level repair or deep disassembly unless authorized and supported by applicable service procedures.

steps.title: Correct External Causes and Verify Operation
steps.instructions: Correct identified external issues through approved repair practice, then clear or acknowledge the fault as permitted. Re-enable iBED Awareness, verify siderail-status recognition, confirm no related scale or Awareness error returns, and complete applicable functional checks before returning the bed to service.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Turn off Awareness - Call Service while iBED Awareness was enabled. Awareness indicators could not be considered reliable for patient monitoring.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed Turn off Awareness - Call Service message while iBED Awareness was enabled. Reviewed the error log for an Awareness-related scale/load-cell or siderail-switch fault and inspected for external interference, visible damage, connector condition, and abnormal siderail operation.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the identified external condition affecting the Awareness subsystem, verified siderail-status recognition and applicable scale function, re-enabled iBED Awareness, and confirmed the message did not return. Bed passed functional verification and was returned to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 904 Unknown Bed Type
description: Troubleshooting Error 904 Unknown Bed Type, which occurs when the Stryker S3 detects an unrecognized bed-type configuration value and may stop all bed functions.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the Stryker S3 bed from patient use if Unknown Bed Type - Call Service is displayed or bed functions are unavailable. Transfer any patient to a known-working bed before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display shows Unknown Bed Type - Call Service. Document whether the message occurs at startup, remains continuous or intermittent, and whether all bed functions are unavailable.

steps.title: Check Power Source and External Condition
steps.instructions: Verify a known-working power source and inspect the power cord, plug, visible wiring, control panels, covers, and external condition for damage, impact, contamination, or evidence of recent service.

steps.title: Confirm the Failure Is Not a Simple Control or Lockout Condition
steps.instructions: With the bed removed from patient use, perform basic safe functional checks to confirm that the issue is not caused by a control lockout, disconnected pendant, or isolated failed movement control.

steps.title: Review Bed Type and Installed Configuration Information
steps.instructions: Where accessible through the approved service information screen, review the identified bed type and installed options. Compare displayed configuration information with the actual Stryker S3 bed and installed features.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible Configuration-Related Connections
steps.instructions: Following facility safety procedures, inspect accessible connectors and harnesses associated with bed identification or recent electronics service. Check for loose seating, damage, contamination, or improper reassembly without proceeding into unauthorized internal repair.

steps.title: Correct an Identified Authorized Configuration or Connection Issue
steps.instructions: Correct any identified accessible connection or authorized configuration issue within Clinical Engineering scope. Cycle power as appropriate and verify whether Unknown Bed Type - Call Service clears.

steps.title: Perform Functional Verification Before Returning to Service
steps.instructions: If the error clears, verify all installed and applicable bed functions, including movement, articulation, hi-low, siderail indicators, brake status, scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness when applicable. Confirm the error does not recur.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Error 904 Unknown Bed Type - Call Service at startup. Bed functions were unavailable while the error message was active.
CCR.Cause: Bed software detected an unrecognized configuration value. Power source, visible condition, basic controls, and accessible configuration-related connections were checked; error remained active, indicating a configuration or controlling electronics fault requiring further evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from patient use, labeled unit Out of Service, verified external checks and accessible connections, and referred bed for bench evaluation/repair due to persistent Error 904 and unavailable functions.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 207 Zero Fail
description: Troubleshooting Error 207 Zero Fail when unstable scale zeroing makes Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions unreliable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use if Error 207 Call Service is present and Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness functions are required. Transfer the patient to a safe, known-working bed before troubleshooting and do not rely on affected monitoring or weighing functions.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display reports Error 207 Call Service and document whether the error occurs during zeroing, after bed movement or accessory changes, or intermittently while stationary. Note unreliable weight, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness behavior.

steps.title: Confirm the Bed Is Properly Unloaded for Zeroing
steps.instructions: Remove the patient and address unintended loading from accessories, linens, bags, pumps, drainage tubing, cords, hoses, cables, or nearby equipment before retrying the scale zero procedure.

steps.title: Inspect for External Contact or Mechanical Interference
steps.instructions: Check the bed frame, siderails, caster areas, attached lines, and surrounding equipment for contact, binding, debris, tension, visible damage, contamination, or lodged objects affecting the weighing structure.

steps.title: Verify Stable Bed Position and Basic Operating Conditions
steps.instructions: Place the bed on a firm, level surface, confirm it is not rocking or shifting, verify reliable power, note additional errors, and allow the bed to remain stationary before zeroing.

steps.title: Review Scale Information and Retry the Applicable Procedure
steps.instructions: Use the appropriate Maintenance Menu function to review scale-system information, then retry the applicable zero procedure with the bed unloaded, stable, and free of interference. Document the result and any additional scale or load-cell errors.

steps.title: Check Accessible Scale-System Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible scale-system wiring and connectors for obvious damage, pinching, contamination, looseness, or disconnection. Do not perform unauthorized internal component or board-level repair.

steps.title: Verify Function Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: After correction, confirm Error 207 does not return, verify scale operation, verify Bed Exit and iBED Awareness functions as appropriate, and document the corrective action before returning the bed to service.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displays Error 207 Call Service / Zero Fail during scale zeroing. Scale will not obtain a stable zero value; Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions are considered unreliable.
CCR.Cause: Bed inspected unloaded and stationary. No external frame contact, cable tension, caster obstruction, accessory interference, or unstable positioning found. Error remained after applicable zero procedure was retried, indicating a likely scale-system, load-cell, wiring, or electronics failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from clinical service, labeled Out of Service, and routed for further scale-system bench evaluation or repair. Staff advised not to rely on Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness functions while fault is present.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 206 CS5533 Fatal Communication Error
description: Troubleshooting Error 206 CS5533 Fatal Communication Error, a communication failure that may make Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions unreliable or unavailable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use if Error 206 Call Service is active. Do not rely on Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness while the error is present. Transfer any patient to a known-working bed before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Associated Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm Error 206 Call Service on the display with the bed out of clinical use. Document when it appears, whether it is constant or intermittent, which affected functions are abnormal, and whether additional errors are logged.

steps.title: Check the Bed's Basic Operating Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm connection to a known-good power source and normal power-up. Inspect externally for impact damage, fluid intrusion, contamination, damaged covers, exposed wiring, heat, odor, or abnormal sounds.

steps.title: Confirm the Affected Features Are Not Safe to Use
steps.instructions: Without placing the bed into patient service, observe the Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions. Treat these features as unreliable while Error 206 remains active, even if operation appears temporarily normal.

steps.title: Review the Error Log
steps.instructions: Review the Error Log according to approved Clinical Engineering procedure. Look for repeated Error 206 occurrences and related scale, load-cell, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness errors.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible Scale-System Connections and Wiring
steps.instructions: With the bed removed from service and power managed appropriately, inspect accessible scale-system wiring and connections for loose connectors, damaged harnesses, contamination, corrosion, or fluid intrusion. Reseat only accessible connections allowed by procedure and service guidance.

steps.title: Check for Mechanical or Environmental Contributors
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible frame and load-cell-related areas for impact, twisting, cable rubbing, cable strain, debris, contamination, or fluid exposure without performing internal disassembly.

steps.title: Recheck the Error After Correcting Any External Issue
steps.instructions: After correcting any external concern, power the bed according to service procedure and determine whether Error 206 returns. Verify Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness operation before return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Error 206 Call Service / CS5533 Fatal Communication Error. Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions were considered unreliable due to the reported communication fault.
CCR.Cause: Inspected bed for external damage, contamination, power concerns, accessible scale-system wiring issues, and loose accessible connections. Error 206 remained active after external checks, indicating a likely internal load-cell communication failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from clinical service and labeled Out of Service. Referred unit for bench evaluation and repair. Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness verification required after repair before return to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 201 Head Left Load Cell
description: Troubleshooting Error 201 / Head Left Load Cell, which indicates an abnormal head-left load-cell reading and can make the bed's scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions unreliable or unavailable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use if Error 201 Call Service is displayed or if the scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness functions cannot be trusted. Transfer any active patient to another appropriate bed before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display shows Error 201 Call Service and document whether it occurs at startup, after loading or repositioning, or intermittently. Record any associated scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness concerns.

steps.title: Confirm the Bed Is Properly Positioned and Unloaded for Evaluation
steps.instructions: Move the bed to a safe evaluation area, remove unnecessary loading from the weighing surface, and confirm the bed is stable, level, and not contacting objects that could apply abnormal force to the frame.

steps.title: Inspect the Head-Left Load-Cell Area for Interference or Binding
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible head-left load-cell location and surrounding frame area for debris, contamination, displaced components, foreign objects, binding, or visible frame interference. Do not perform internal disassembly during initial troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible Wiring and Connections Associated With the Head-Left Position
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible cable routing and connections for looseness, disconnection, pinching, stretching, crushed insulation, cuts, abrasions, contamination, or damage from bed movement.

steps.title: Use the Maintenance Menu to Confirm Load-Cell Diagnostic Information
steps.instructions: View the available load-cell diagnostic information and determine whether Load Cell Error with HL is identified. Record the diagnostic result in the work order.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Fault Clears After External Corrections
steps.instructions: Correct any identified interference, binding, debris, or accessible connection issue and repeat the diagnostic check. If the HL fault remains after external checks, remove the bed from service for repair-level evaluation.

steps.title: Recalibrate and Function-Test After Correction or Repair
steps.instructions: After correction or completed repair, perform approved scale recalibration and verify normal scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness operation. Confirm Error 201 no longer appears.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the bed to clinical use only after the error has cleared, HL diagnostic status is normal, recalibration is successful, and all affected functions pass verification.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Error 201 Call Service. Staff reported concern for unreliable scale and Bed Exit/iBED Awareness operation.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found mechanical interference at the head-left load-cell area causing abnormal HL load-cell diagnostic status. Error indicated the head-left load-cell reading was outside expected range.
CCR.Resolution: Removed interference, verified accessible cable condition and connections, performed scale recalibration, and completed functional testing of scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness. Error 201 no longer displayed; bed returned to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 202 Head Right Load Cell
description: Troubleshooting Error 202, indicating a head-right load-cell range fault that may affect scale accuracy, Bed Exit monitoring, and iBED Awareness reliability.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use if Error 202 Call Service is displayed or if Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness functions are needed for care. Transfer the patient to a known-working bed before troubleshooting and do not rely on affected monitoring or weighing functions until verified.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Associated Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display reports Error 202 Call Service. Document when the error appears and whether scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness symptoms are present.

steps.title: Check Bed Setup and External Interference
steps.instructions: Place the bed on a level surface and check for contact with walls, equipment, cords, furniture, trapped items, linens, straps, or accessories that may create abnormal loading at the head-right corner.

steps.title: Inspect the Head-Right Load-Cell Area
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the head-right sensing area, surrounding frame, visible wiring, and accessible connectors for damage, binding, contamination, looseness, misalignment, or cable problems without performing internal disassembly.

steps.title: Check Accessories and External Loading Conditions
steps.instructions: Remove unnecessary removable accessories or stored equipment that could unevenly load the bed. Confirm the patient surface and attached components are positioned normally, then power cycle and retest.

steps.title: Review Load-Cell Diagnostic Information
steps.instructions: With the bed out of service, review applicable load-cell diagnostic information according to approved service procedures and document whether the head-right sensing path is identified, such as an HR indication.

steps.title: Determine Whether an External Cause Was Corrected
steps.instructions: If an external obstruction, abnormal loading condition, or accessible connection issue clears the error, continue with functional verification. If visible damage or persistent head-right indications remain, escalate for repair.

steps.title: Verify Operation After Correction or Repair
steps.instructions: Confirm error-free power-up and verify scale accuracy, Bed Exit setup and alarm operation, and iBED Awareness function before returning the bed to service.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the bed to service only after the error is cleared and all affected functions pass verification. Otherwise remove it from service, label it Out of Service, and send it for repair or bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Error 202 Call Service - Head Right Load Cell. Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions were considered unreliable while the error was active.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed Error 202 Call Service. No external frame interference or abnormal loading was found. Load-cell diagnostic information identified the HR sensing path, indicating a likely head-right load-cell or related circuit fault.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from patient use, labeled Out of Service, and referred for bench repair. Required scale recalibration and verification of Bed Exit and iBED Awareness operation before return to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 203 Foot Left Load Cell
description: Troubleshooting Error 203 from a foot-left load-cell fault that can make Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness operation unreliable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the Stryker S3 bed from patient use while Error 203 Call Service is present. Do not rely on Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness functions until the fault is corrected and verified. Transfer any patient to a known-working bed before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Associated Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display shows Error 203 Call Service. Document whether the error occurs at startup, after loading or unloading, during scale operation, or intermittently. Note unreliable weight readings, Bed Exit concerns, iBED Awareness concerns, or a diagnostic Load Cell Error — FL indication.

steps.title: Check the Bed Setup and External Conditions
steps.instructions: With the bed unloaded and removed from patient use, inspect for equipment, cords, linens, bags, floor obstructions, walls, nearby equipment, or abnormal loading contacting the frame or foot-left corner. Remove external interference and retest.

steps.title: Inspect the Foot-Left Load-Cell Area
steps.instructions: Inspect the foot-left load-cell location for visible binding, restricted movement, bent or displaced components, debris, contamination, impact damage, or frame interference. Do not perform internal disassembly outside approved service procedures.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible Wiring and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible foot-left load-cell wiring for loose connectors, damaged cables, pinching, stretching, abrasion, poor routing, fluid contamination, or connector damage. Correct safely addressable external issues and retest.

steps.title: Review Load-Cell Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Use the appropriate maintenance diagnostic function to confirm whether Load Cell Error — FL is present. Compare with other load-cell positions when available to determine whether the fault is isolated to the foot-left corner.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Fault Has Been Isolated
steps.instructions: Determine whether the error resulted from external interference, mechanical binding, physical damage, a cable or connection issue, or a likely failed foot-left load cell. Persistent faults after external checks require repair evaluation.

steps.title: Verify Function After Correction or Repair
steps.instructions: Confirm that Error 203 Call Service no longer appears. Complete scale calibration as required, scale functional verification, Bed Exit functional checks, iBED Awareness functional checks, and a general bed safety and operational inspection.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: When the error has cleared and all required functional checks pass, document the repair and return the bed to service according to facility procedure. Do not continue troubleshooting a resolved condition.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Error 203 Call Service. Reported fault identified as Load Cell Error — FL, affecting Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness reliability.
CCR.Cause: Inspection identified interference at the foot-left load-cell area causing abnormal load-cell readings; after removal, diagnostics no longer indicated Load Cell Error — FL.
CCR.Resolution: Removed interference from the foot-left load-cell area, inspected accessible wiring and mechanical condition, performed scale calibration and functional verification of Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness systems. Error cleared and bed returned to service.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 204 Foot Right Load Cell
description: Troubleshooting Error 204 Foot Right Load Cell, indicating an unreliable foot-right load-cell signal affecting Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from patient use if the Scale, Bed Exit, or iBED Awareness function is needed for safe patient care. Do not rely on patient weight readings, Bed Exit monitoring, or iBED Awareness status while this error is present. Transfer the patient to a known-working bed or provide alternate fall-prevention and monitoring measures before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the bed displays Error 204 Call Service and document whether the condition occurs at startup, during scale use, when activating Bed Exit, or while iBED Awareness is enabled. Review available load-cell diagnostics and confirm whether Load Cell Error with FR is displayed.

steps.title: Inspect the Bed for External Mechanical Interference
steps.instructions: Inspect the foot-right weighing area for caught linens, straps, cables, accessories, nearby equipment contact, floor obstructions, debris, contamination, bent components, visible binding, or an unstable bed position. Correct external interference and recheck the error.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible Foot-Right Load-Cell Wiring and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible wiring and connectors for loose seating, pinching, cuts, stretching, corrosion, fluid intrusion, poor harness routing, or visible damage. Reseat accessible connections and secure incorrectly routed wiring as appropriate.

steps.title: Recheck Load-Cell Diagnostics
steps.instructions: After correcting any external interference or connection issue, recheck load-cell diagnostic information. Determine whether the FR fault clears or remains specific to the foot-right load-cell position.

steps.title: Verify Scale System Calibration and Function if the Error Clears
steps.instructions: After correction or repair, perform the applicable scale calibration according to approved service instructions. Verify stable scale readings with an appropriate known test weight, verify Bed Exit and iBED Awareness operation as equipped, and confirm that Error 204 does not return.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: When Error 204 is no longer active and Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions have passed applicable testing, document the repair and return the bed to service.

CCR.Complaint: Stryker S3 hospital bed displayed Error 204 Call Service. Load-cell diagnostics identified the foot-right position as FR Load Cell Error. Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness functions were considered unreliable while the fault was active.
CCR.Cause: Foot-right load-cell fault remained after checking for frame interference, binding, contamination, and accessible wiring or connector issues, indicating a likely failed foot-right load cell or associated scale-system component.
CCR.Resolution: Removed bed from service and labeled Out of Service for repair of the foot-right load-cell system. Scale calibration and verification of Scale, Bed Exit, and iBED Awareness operation are required before return to clinical use.

title: Stryker S3 Hospital Bed - Error: 090 Brake Switch Error
description: Troubleshooting Error 090 Brake Switch Error, indicating unreliable brake-status sensing due to disconnected or shorted brake-switch wiring that may affect safe bed braking verification.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the Stryker S3 bed from patient use if brake operation or brake-status indication cannot be trusted. If occupied, coordinate transfer to a known-safe bed before troubleshooting. Apply the brakes manually and physically verify that the bed does not roll.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Associated Behavior
