If prior use or exposed adhesive is confirmed: Replace the electrode set and stop if device readiness returns to normal. Do not attempt to restore used therapeutic electrodes for standby service.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Electrode Lead and Accessible Connection Area
steps.instructions: Check externally accessible portions for: Cuts; Pinching; Abrasion; Kinks; Crushed insulation; Pulled strain relief; Bent or damaged connector features; Contamination; Loose seating. Do not probe electrical contacts or disassemble the CR2. Expected: The lead and accessible connection area are intact and properly seated. If damage is found: Replace the electrode set with a verified compatible set.

steps.title: 8. Verify Correct Installation and Seating
steps.instructions: Confirm that the replacement electrode set is installed according to the CR2 electrode-replacement configuration. Check that: The electrode assembly sits correctly; The lead is not trapped or pinched; The connector is fully seated; The cover closes normally; No foreign material prevents proper installation. Expected: The electrode assembly is correctly installed without cable stress or obstruction. If reseating or correcting installation resolves the readiness concern: Document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 9. Install a Known-Good, In-Date Replacement Set
steps.instructions: When the original set is opened, damaged, expired, suspect, or cannot be verified, install a known-good replacement CR2-compatible electrode set. After replacement: Confirm correct seating; Close the device normally; Observe the CR2 readiness indication; Allow the device to complete its normal readiness behavior; Check for abnormal audible or visual indications. A flashing readiness indicator is identified in Stryker CR2 operating information as the normal ready-for-use condition. Expected: The CR2 returns to its normal ready indication with the verified replacement electrode set. If resolved: Remove the questionable electrode set from usable inventory, document the replacement, and stop.

steps.title: 10. Check for Storage or Environmental Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED location and carrying environment for conditions that may have damaged the electrode set: Water exposure; Excessive heat; Direct sunlight; Freezing conditions; Crushing by stored objects; Sharp cabinet edges; Chemical exposure; Repeated cable pinching; Poorly secured transport. Expected: Storage conditions do not explain repeated package damage. If an external storage cause is identified: Correct the storage issue before returning the CR2 to service.

steps.title: 11. Reassess Device Readiness After Electrode Replacement
steps.instructions: With a verified compatible, undamaged, in-date electrode set installed: Confirm normal standby condition; Observe the readiness indicator; Check for persistent abnormal indications; Review remote readiness status when the facility uses the applicable connected AED-management workflow; Confirm the AED remains properly stocked and accessible. Expected: The device indicates normal readiness. If the problem is resolved: Return the unit to service according to facility procedure and document the completed electrode replacement.

steps.title: 12. Stop if the Readiness Concern Persists With Known-Good Electrodes
steps.instructions: If the LIFEPAK CR2 continues to show an abnormal readiness condition after installation of a verified compatible, undamaged, in-date electrode set, do not continue swapping consumables indefinitely. At this point, common external electrode causes have been substantially ruled out. Expected: The unit is escalated for controlled evaluation rather than returned to emergency service with unresolved readiness.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 electrode package was open and the AED could not be confirmed ready for emergency use.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the installed QUIK-STEP electrode package compromised with the protective system already disturbed; no external CR2 damage was observed.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the compromised electrodes, installed a verified compatible in-date replacement set, confirmed proper seating and normal readiness indication, and returned the AED to service.

helpfulDetails: Removed electrode lot information, if required by facility process

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Connect Electrodes Prompt Remains Active
description: Troubleshooting a persistent Connect Electrodes prompt caused by pad application, electrode condition, patient contact, packaging, or likely internal detection faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting during an active resuscitation. If the LIFEPAK CR2 continues prompting to connect electrodes despite correct pad application, immediately provide another verified defibrillator/AED and continue care according to clinical protocol. Expected: Patient care is not delayed by an AED that cannot reliably detect applied electrodes. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 uses audible and visual guidance during rescue operation, and unresolved electrode detection can prevent normal rhythm-analysis and therapy progression. If another device resolves the immediate clinical concern, stop troubleshooting on the patient and evaluate the affected CR2 in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Reproduce or document the complaint without unnecessarily consuming a serviceable electrode set. Determine whether: The prompt begins normally before pad placement but never clears; The prompt is intermittent; One or both pads were visibly loose; The electrodes were previously opened or used; The electrode package or tray was damaged; The issue occurred only during one rescue event; The unit shows additional abnormal prompts, indicators, or tones. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to a persistent electrode-contact problem versus a broader device malfunction. If the reported prompt cleared after correcting an obvious application issue and the device subsequently performs normally, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Electrode Type
steps.instructions: Confirm that the installed electrodes are the correct LIFEPAK CR2 QUIK-STEP electrodes and are approved for the device. Stryker identifies the CR2 electrode set as QUIK-STEP pacing/ECG/defibrillation electrodes; Stryker’s current CR2 product information lists one set with the device. Check for: Incorrect LIFEPAK-family electrodes; Trainer electrodes; Noncompatible substitutes; Improvised adapters or connections. Expected: Genuine, correct CR2-compatible electrodes are present. If incorrect electrodes caused the issue, replace them with the proper approved set, restore the device according to facility policy, document the correction, and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Electrode Condition and Expiration
steps.instructions: Inspect the electrode assembly externally. Check for: Expired electrodes; Previously opened or deployed pads; Torn packaging; Damaged lead conductors; Contamination; Dried or compromised adhesive/gel; Visible physical damage. Stryker cautions against using damaged, expired, or dried-out pads and notes that CR2 QUIK-STEP electrodes should not be opened until immediately before use. Stryker currently lists the CR2 QUIK-STEP replacement set with a four-year shelf life. Expected: Electrodes are within expiration, unopened before use, physically intact, and suitable for deployment. If the electrode set is expired, opened, damaged, or otherwise questionable, replace it with an approved in-date set. If that resolves the complaint, document and stop.

steps.title: 5. Review Pad Application and Full Skin Contact
steps.instructions: For the actual reported event, verify whether both pads were applied in the illustrated locations and were fully adhered to the patient. Look for possible causes such as: Pad only partially contacting skin; Folded adhesive surface; Clothing trapped beneath a pad; Excessive chest hair preventing adhesion; Moisture interfering with contact; Pad placed over another material; Pads touching or overlapping. Stryker specifically instructs that pads should adhere completely to skin and should not touch each other or other material on the patient’s chest. Expected: Both pads had broad, direct, secure patient contact. If correcting pad contact clears the prompt, the issue was external. Stop and document the cause.

steps.title: 6. Check for Patient-Specific Contact Factors
steps.instructions: Review whether the failure may have been unique to the patient rather than the CR2. Consider: Very wet skin; Heavy chest hair; Significant movement; Poor adhesion due to body contour; Extremely small patient anatomy; Pads becoming displaced during CPR or transport. For small children where standard placement risks pad contact or overlap, Stryker describes anterior-posterior placement guidance. Expected: The event history either identifies a plausible patient-contact problem or supports a true equipment complaint. If evidence strongly indicates poor contact during the event and no device abnormality remains, document the finding and return the device only after the required readiness checks are satisfactory.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Electrode Tray and Accessible Interface Area
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from clinical use, inspect the CR2 electrode storage area and all externally accessible portions of the electrode assembly. Check for: Electrode tray not properly seated; Cover or packaging displaced; Pinched lead conductors; Visible contamination; Foreign material; Cracked or damaged accessible components; Evidence of impact or fluid intrusion. Do not open the defibrillator housing or perform unauthorized internal disassembly. Expected: The electrode assembly is correctly installed and no external mechanical damage is visible. If reseating an approved replaceable electrode assembly according to facility-authorized practice corrects an obvious installation issue, complete the required post-service verification, document, and stop.

steps.title: 8. Evaluate With a Known-Good, Approved Electrode Set When Justified
steps.instructions: If the original electrodes are suspect, replace them with a known-good, in-date CR2 QUIK-STEP electrode set using approved replacement practice. Do not repeatedly deploy consumable pads solely for exploratory testing. Follow facility policy and manufacturer-authorized test methods. Stryker identifies CR2 QUIK-STEP electrodes as the dedicated replacement consumable for the device. Expected: A defective or compromised electrode assembly is either confirmed or ruled out. If replacing a suspect electrode set restores normal operation, document the failed consumable and stop.

steps.title: 9. Check for Broader Device Readiness Abnormalities
steps.instructions: Inspect the CR2 readiness indication and note any additional alert behavior. Determine whether the device also shows: Abnormal readiness status; Repeating alert tones; Unexpected startup behavior; Additional voice prompts; Evidence of battery or self-test concern. Stryker’s CR2 operating information describes the readiness indicator as part of routine readiness assessment and instructs checking prompt behavior during inspection. Expected: No unrelated readiness or startup abnormalities are present. If multiple abnormalities exist, treat the complaint as a broader device fault rather than an isolated electrode issue.

steps.title: 10. Perform Only Facility-Authorized Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After external causes are ruled out, perform the CR2 functional or performance verification available to Clinical Engineering under your facility’s approved procedures and authorized Stryker service resources. Do not improvise patient simulations or defeat safety features. Expected: The unit either recognizes the approved test condition normally or the electrode-detection complaint remains reproducible. If the Connect Electrodes prompt remains active despite correct approved electrodes and verified external conditions, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 repeatedly announced “Connect Electrodes” after the pads were applied during use.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the installed QUIK-STEP electrode set was expired and showed compromised pad adhesion, preventing reliable patient contact.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the expired electrode set, installed an approved in-date LIFEPAK CR2 QUIK-STEP set, verified satisfactory device readiness, and returned the AED to service.

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Poor Electrode Contact or Check Electrodes Prompt
description: Troubleshooting repeated electrode-contact prompts caused by poor skin contact, patient preparation, pad condition, tray seating, or a persistent device-side connection fault.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay resuscitation for extended equipment troubleshooting. During an active cardiac arrest response: Continue CPR according to the emergency response protocol. Follow the LIFEPAK CR2 voice prompts. Correct only immediately visible pad-contact or connection issues. Obtain another verified AED or defibrillator without delay if the CR2 cannot establish dependable electrode contact or deliver required therapy. Expected: Resuscitation continues without being dependent on prolonged troubleshooting of a malfunctioning AED. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 operating instructions identify poor pad adhesion and inadequate electrode-tray connection as causes of electrode-related prompts. The device manufacturer also directs responders to continue CPR when required shock delivery is not possible. If the immediate clinical situation has been transferred to another functional device, continue evaluation only in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Prompt and Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine what Clinical Engineering or staff actually observed. Document whether the device announced: “CHECK PADS FOR GOOD CONTACT TO BARE SKIN”; “CHECK ELECTRODE TRAY CONNECTION”; An intermittent contact-related prompt; Failure to progress normally after pad application; Loss of contact only when the patient or cable moved. Also determine: Whether both pads were fully applied; Whether the prompt began immediately or during use; Whether the electrode tray had already been opened; Whether the pads were expired, damaged, or previously used. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to patient-to-pad contact, electrode condition, tray connection, or a persistent device fault. Why it matters: Stryker’s published CR2 troubleshooting table specifically links these prompts to improper pad adhesion or inadequate connection of the electrode tray to the defibrillator.

steps.title: 3. Check Patient Skin Preparation During the Reported Event
steps.instructions: For an active event, correct only what can be done immediately without delaying CPR or defibrillation. Verify whether the pad locations were: Bare; Clean; Dry; Free of excessive hair that prevented adhesion; Free of clothing, dressings, medication patches, or other material beneath the pad. If excessive hair prevents adhesion and a razor is immediately available, quickly clear the required area. Dry or clean the skin as necessary and firmly reapply the pads. Expected: Each pad lies flat and adheres completely to prepared bare skin. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 instructions direct users to clean, shave, and dry the skin when necessary and firmly press the pads onto the patient. If the prompt clears, the problem was likely inadequate patient-to-electrode contact. Stop troubleshooting and continue the clinical response.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pad Adhesion Across the Entire Surface
steps.instructions: Check both electrodes for: Lifted edges; Wrinkles; Air pockets; Partial contact; Folding; Contamination; Loss of adhesion caused by moisture, hair, or body contour. Press firmly across the entire pad surface without disturbing correct placement. Expected: Both electrodes remain fully adhered with no obvious gaps or lifted areas. Why it matters: Stryker warns that incomplete adhesion and air pockets can contribute to ineffective energy delivery and skin burns. If full adhesion clears the prompt, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify Correct Pad Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm the pads are positioned according to the illustrations printed on the LIFEPAK CR2 electrodes. Check that: Adult placement matches the pad graphics; Pads do not overlap or touch each other; Pads are not directly over an implanted pacemaker or ICD; Pediatric placement is appropriate for the patient’s size and prevents pad-to-pad contact. Expected: Electrode placement is appropriate and the pads remain separated with full skin contact. Stryker’s instructions state that pads should be applied as illustrated and pressed firmly to achieve complete adhesion; for small children, the pads should be positioned so they do not touch. If correcting placement resolves the prompt, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check Electrode Tray Seating
steps.instructions: Once the device is off-patient and available for controlled evaluation, inspect the QUIK-STEP electrode tray externally. Verify that: The tray is fully inserted; The front corners are seated; The tray is not visibly raised or partially disengaged; No obvious debris or physical obstruction prevents seating; The tray appears mechanically secure. Do not force a damaged tray or connector area. Expected: The electrode tray is fully and evenly seated in the defibrillator. Why it matters: Stryker identifies incomplete electrode-tray insertion as a cause of the CR2 electrode-tray connection prompt. If proper seating resolves the issue and subsequent approved readiness checks pass, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Electrode Tray Condition and Use-By Date
steps.instructions: Check the installed tray for: Broken seal; Evidence it was previously opened; Prior use; Passed Use By date; Visible tray damage; Evidence of dried or compromised electrodes. The CR2 electrode tray should be replaced if the seal is broken, the electrodes have been used, or the Use By date has passed. Expected: The installed tray is sealed, unused, undamaged, and within date. If the tray is compromised, replace it with the correct compatible electrode tray according to approved facility and manufacturer procedures, then verify readiness. Stop if the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Electrode Tray When Authorized
steps.instructions: If the original tray is suspect and facility procedures permit, install a known-good, in-date, sealed, compatible LIFEPAK CR2 electrode tray. Inspect the replacement before installation: Seal intact; Within Use By date; No visible damage. After installation, confirm that the tray is fully seated. Expected: The device recognizes the known-good electrode tray and no connection-related abnormal condition remains. The manufacturer’s instructions describe the QUIK-STEP electrode assembly as a replaceable tray and require inspection of the seal and Use By date before installation. If a known-good tray resolves the issue, document the original electrode tray as the probable cause and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Verify Device Readiness
steps.instructions: After restoring the AED to its normal ready configuration: Close the lid; Observe the Readiness indicator; Confirm expected ready behavior; If readiness is abnormal, use only the manufacturer-approved readiness-status procedure and follow the resulting prompts. Stryker states that after electrode replacement and lid closure, the Readiness indicator should flash every six seconds; if it does not, the device provides a button-based status check to identify whether it is ready. Expected: The AED returns to documented ready status with a correctly installed electrode tray. If readiness is normal and the complaint is resolved, return the device to service only after completing required facility inspection and documentation.

steps.title: 10. Stop if the Prompt Persists With a Known-Good Tray
steps.instructions: If the CR2 continues to report electrode-contact or electrode-tray connection problems after: External condition checks; Correct tray seating; Inspection for damage; Use of a verified compatible replacement tray; Approved readiness verification. do not proceed into internal connector, circuit, impedance-sensing, or board-level repair unless specifically authorized and trained under the applicable service program. Expected: A persistent problem is treated as a probable internal or device-side fault rather than repeatedly attributed to external electrodes. If unresolved, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 repeatedly announced a poor pad-contact or electrode-tray connection prompt during use.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the QUIK-STEP electrode tray was not fully seated in the defibrillator, causing intermittent electrode connection recognition.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the electrode tray, verified secure installation and normal device readiness indication, completed required functional checks, and returned the AED to service.

helpfulDetails: Removed from service or returned to service

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Adult or Pediatric Mode Selection Failure
description: Troubleshooting failure to enter, indicate, maintain, or return from Child Mode due to operation, button access, contamination, power, or control faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended mode-selection troubleshooting while the LIFEPAK CR2 is being relied upon during an active resuscitation. If the required adult or pediatric operating mode cannot be confidently selected, immediately provide another verified defibrillator/AED and follow facility emergency-response procedures. Expected: Patient care is transferred to equipment with confirmed operating readiness and appropriate therapy capability. Why it matters: On the LIFEPAK CR2, the CHILD MODE button changes therapy to reduced energy levels and adjusts CPR coaching for pediatric use. An uncertain mode-selection condition can therefore affect therapy configuration. If patient care has been transferred safely, continue troubleshooting only in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the LIFEPAK CR2 in a controlled environment and determine exactly what is occurring. Check whether: The CHILD MODE button produces no response; The unit does not announce or indicate a mode change; Child Mode activates only intermittently; The unit enters Child Mode but will not return to Adult Mode; The button appears physically stuck or obstructed; The problem occurs only during a particular stage of operation; Other controls or voice prompts are also abnormal. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to a reproducible mode-selection, user-interface, power, or broader device fault. Why it matters: Stryker documents that pressing the CHILD MODE button switches between adult and child operation; pressing it again returns the unit to Adult Mode. If normal switching is confirmed repeatedly, the original complaint may have involved operation, timing, or an intermittent condition. Document findings and continue readiness verification before return to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify Correct Mode-Selection Operation
steps.instructions: Using the approved operating instructions and without connecting the unit to a patient, operate the LIFEPAK CR2 and press the CHILD MODE button as intended. Observe for the expected mode-change response. Then press the button again and confirm return to Adult Mode. Expected: The device consistently changes to Child Mode and then back to Adult Mode. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 uses a dedicated CHILD MODE button rather than requiring separate pediatric electrodes for mode selection. Stryker identifies the CR2 QUIK-STEP electrodes as usable for adult and pediatric patients. If correct mode switching is restored and remains repeatable, stop troubleshooting and complete required functional/readiness checks before return to service.

steps.title: 4. Check for External Button Obstruction or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the CHILD MODE button and surrounding housing. Look for: Dried fluid; Cleaning residue; Adhesive contamination; Debris around the button edge; Damaged overlay material; Cracked housing; Evidence of impact; Button binding or abnormal feel. Clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer-compatible procedures. Do not flood the control area with liquid or force tools around the button. Expected: The button surface is clean, unobstructed, intact, and mechanically usable from the exterior. If cleaning removes an obstruction and normal mode switching returns consistently, stop troubleshooting after completing readiness checks.

steps.title: 5. Compare Button Response With Other Device Functions
steps.instructions: Observe whether the LIFEPAK CR2 otherwise starts and operates normally. Check for: Normal startup behavior; Clear voice prompts; Expected status indications; Response from other accessible controls; Unexpected restart or shutdown; Abnormal warning indications. Expected: Clinical Engineering determines whether the failure is isolated to mode selection or part of a broader user-interface or device-control problem. Why it matters: Multiple abnormal controls or startup behaviors make an isolated external CHILD MODE button issue less likely. If broader abnormal operation is present, remove the device from service and escalate for evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Check Battery and General Power Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the installed battery condition and confirm the device shows no obvious evidence of unstable power. Look for: Low-battery indication; Unexpected shutdown; Intermittent startup; Restart when controls are operated; Battery not fully seated; Battery or battery-compartment damage. Reseat or replace the battery only when permitted by facility procedure and with the correct approved component. Expected: The unit powers consistently without resets, dropouts, or abnormal battery indications. If correcting an external battery seating or known battery condition restores reliable mode selection, stop troubleshooting after completing required readiness verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Device for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Examine the LIFEPAK CR2 exterior for evidence of: Drops; Cracked enclosure; Deformation near the control panel; Liquid intrusion; Damaged button membrane; Loose external components; Heat damage; Chemical attack from cleaning agents. Expected: No physical condition is present that could compromise mode selection or device reliability. If physical damage is found near the control interface, do not continue repeated operational testing as a substitute for repair evaluation. Remove the unit from service.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Mode-Selection Test
steps.instructions: With the device in a controlled Clinical Engineering environment, repeat the Adult-to-Child and Child-to-Adult selection sequence several times. Confirm that: Each intentional button press is recognized; Child Mode activates consistently; Adult Mode returns consistently; No intermittent missed presses occur; No abnormal resets or prompt interruptions occur. Expected: Mode selection is repeatable and dependable. If the failure occurs even once during controlled repeat testing, treat the issue as intermittent and unresolved. Do not return the AED to service based on temporary recovery.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good LIFEPAK CR2 When Available
steps.instructions: If facility inventory permits, compare the affected unit with another verified LIFEPAK CR2. Compare: Button travel and feel; Response timing; Voice or mode-change behavior; Startup behavior; Reliability of repeated switching. Do not use the comparison unit as justification to alter internal adjustments. Expected: Clinical Engineering determines whether the affected device behaves abnormally relative to a known-good unit. If the affected unit remains inconsistent, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Readiness Verification
steps.instructions: If the issue appears resolved, complete the facility-approved post-service readiness and functional checks appropriate for the LIFEPAK CR2. Confirm: Normal device readiness; Reliable mode selection; Normal status indication; No unresolved battery warning; Electrodes are present, compatible, and within expiration; No physical damage remains; Device is properly restored for emergency use. Expected: The LIFEPAK CR2 is fully ready for service, not merely temporarily responsive. If readiness cannot be confirmed, remove the device from service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 would not reliably switch from Adult Mode to Child Mode when the CHILD MODE button was pressed.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced intermittent CHILD MODE button response after confirming normal startup, acceptable battery condition, and no external obstruction around the control.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the LIFEPAK CR2 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and routed the unit for repair evaluation due to unreliable adult/pediatric mode selection.

helpfulDetails: Whether return to Adult Mode was confirmed
Evidence of impact or liquid exposure

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - ECG Analysis Will Not Start or Complete
description: Troubleshooting absent, delayed, interrupted, or incomplete ECG rhythm analysis caused by electrode contact, accessories, motion, interference, power, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting on a LIFEPAK CR2 that is required for an active cardiac arrest response. If ECG analysis does not start or complete during actual patient use: Follow the device’s voice and visual prompts; Continue resuscitation according to the facility’s emergency-response protocol; Obtain another verified AED/defibrillator immediately when available; Do not delay CPR or higher-level emergency response while attempting equipment troubleshooting. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on an AED with unresolved rhythm-analysis performance. Why it matters: Failure to complete rhythm analysis may prevent the device from reaching an appropriate shock decision. Troubleshooting beyond immediate external corrections should occur off patient. If another verified defibrillator restores safe emergency-response capability, remove the affected CR2 from clinical reliance and continue evaluation in a controlled setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine precisely what Clinical Engineering can reproduce. Check whether: Analysis never appears to begin; The unit repeatedly instructs the user to attach electrodes; Analysis begins but repeatedly restarts; Analysis remains prolonged; Analysis is interrupted by motion or contact prompts; The unit progresses through CPR prompts but not expected rhythm analysis; The problem occurs only with one electrode set; Voice prompts stop or the operating sequence freezes; The device unexpectedly powers off or restarts. Record all audible prompts, indicator behavior, and sequence timing. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to an electrode-recognition, signal-quality, operating-sequence, power, or device-level problem. If the reported behavior cannot be reproduced, continue with accessory, readiness, and controlled functional checks before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Operating Sequence
steps.instructions: Using an approved non-patient test method, verify that the CR2 is being activated through its normal operating sequence. Check that: The lid opens normally; The device powers on; Voice prompts begin; The device advances through the expected rescue sequence; No startup fault or abnormal readiness indication is present. Do not assume the device should enter rhythm analysis immediately upon power-up. Analysis depends on progression through the AED rescue sequence and acquisition of an acceptable ECG signal through the electrodes. Expected: The CR2 powers on normally and proceeds through its expected prompt sequence. If startup is abnormal, prompts are missing, or the sequence freezes before electrode evaluation, stop and escalate the device for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Check Electrode Connection and Deployment
steps.instructions: Inspect the installed QUIK-STEP electrode assembly and associated connection points externally. Check for: Electrode package damage; Open or compromised packaging; Expired electrodes; Partially deployed electrodes; Visible cable damage; Pinching or severe bends; Loose connection at any user-accessible interface; Evidence of fluid contamination. Ensure the electrode system is installed and routed as intended for the CR2. Expected: The electrode assembly is intact, in date, correctly installed, and free of obvious physical damage. If correcting an obvious seating or deployment problem restores the expected analysis sequence, document the finding, complete required testing, and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Electrode Pad Condition and Contact
steps.instructions: For controlled troubleshooting, use only an approved test setup appropriate for AED evaluation. Do not test rhythm analysis on a healthy person. If reviewing a clinical event, determine whether the pads may have had: Incomplete adhesion; Folded edges; Dried or contaminated conductive surface; Heavy chest hair preventing contact; Moisture between the pad and skin; Incorrect placement; Pads touching or overlapping; Partial removal during movement or CPR. Expected: Both pads can provide stable contact through an approved simulator/test arrangement or were documented as properly applied during the event. Why it matters: The CR2 obtains ECG information through its therapy electrodes. Poor contact can prevent dependable signal acquisition and interfere with analysis. If a known-good compatible electrode set resolves the problem during approved testing, replace the defective or suspect electrode assembly and complete post-service verification.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Electrode Set
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility procedure and manufacturer requirements, repeat the controlled test with a known-good, in-date, compatible electrode set. Do not use visibly damaged, expired, previously deployed, or questionable electrodes for comparison. Expected: The device progresses into and completes the expected analysis sequence with the known-good electrode set. If the problem disappears, the original electrode assembly is the likely cause. Remove the suspect electrodes from service, replace them, document the failure, and complete the required readiness check.

steps.title: 7. Eliminate Motion and Mechanical Disturbance
steps.instructions: During controlled analysis testing: Keep the simulator/test arrangement stationary; Avoid moving the device; Prevent electrode cables from being pulled; Do not manipulate connections during analysis; Ensure the test setup is mechanically stable. When reviewing an actual event, consider: Patient movement; Ongoing transport vibration; Repositioning; Repeated pad disturbance; Mechanical CPR-related conditions; Rescuer contact during a requested hands-off analysis period. Expected: Analysis completes when the ECG input and test setup are stable. If analysis succeeds only when movement stops, document motion or unstable contact as the likely contributor rather than assuming an internal AED failure.

steps.title: 8. Check for Electrical or Electromagnetic Interference
steps.instructions: Move the CR2 and approved test setup away from potential high-interference sources when practical. Consider nearby: Electrosurgical equipment; High-power radio transmitters; Certain telemetry or communication equipment; Large motors; Damaged electrical equipment; Other equipment producing substantial electromagnetic interference. Repeat the controlled test in a different location. Expected: Analysis performance remains stable regardless of location. If the problem occurs only near a specific interference source and clears elsewhere, document the environmental relationship and investigate the source before condemning the AED.

steps.title: 9. Verify Battery and Power Stability
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK CR2 battery externally. Check for: Low-battery indications; Abnormal readiness status; Battery not fully seated; Physical battery damage; Contaminated accessible contacts; Unexpected shutdown; Restart during the rescue sequence; Intermittent operation when the unit is moved. Reseat the battery only when permitted by facility procedure and with the device removed from patient use. Expected: The CR2 remains continuously powered through startup, prompts, ECG acquisition, and analysis testing. If power instability is present, address the battery/power complaint before evaluating analysis performance further.

steps.title: 10. Review Readiness and Self-Monitoring Status
steps.instructions: Check the CR2 readiness indication and any available device-management status information used by the facility. Look for: Not-ready indication; Battery alerts; Electrode alerts; Failed or abnormal self-monitoring status; Unresolved maintenance notifications. Connected CR2 deployments may also provide readiness information through the facility’s configured AED management workflow. Expected: The unit indicates ready status with no unresolved battery, electrode, or device fault. If the AED is not ready or reports a persistent fault, remove it from service and escalate rather than attempting repeated patient-use simulations.

steps.title: 11. Test With an Approved AED/ECG Simulator
steps.instructions: Use a manufacturer-compatible or facility-approved AED analyzer/simulator according to Clinical Engineering procedure. Verify whether the LIFEPAK CR2: Recognizes the connected test load; Enters the expected analysis sequence; Completes analysis on a stable simulated rhythm; Produces an appropriate shock/no-shock decision for the test condition; Repeats the sequence consistently. Use only approved test equipment and established procedures. Do not improvise a live-person test. Expected: The device consistently completes analysis and responds appropriately to the controlled simulated rhythm. If analysis repeatedly fails with a known-good electrode setup and approved simulator, the likelihood of an internal device fault increases.

steps.title: 12. Repeat the Test for Intermittent Failure
steps.instructions: If the first controlled test passes, repeat the sequence enough times to evaluate the reported intermittent behavior. Observe for: Random analysis interruption; Freezing at the same stage; Delayed recognition; Unexpected restart; Prompt sequence failure; Sensitivity to minor device movement; Failure after warming during repeated operation. Expected: Analysis starts and completes consistently across repeated controlled tests. If failure is intermittent but reproducible, remove the unit from service. An intermittent AED analysis problem should not be returned to service solely because one test passed.

steps.title: 13. Inspect for External Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the CR2 externally for: Cracked enclosure; Evidence of impact; Liquid intrusion; Corrosion; Damaged lid mechanism; Damaged battery compartment; Contaminated accessible connections; Unusual heat; Burn odor; Loose internal-sounding components when handled normally. Do not open the enclosure unless specifically authorized, trained, and following approved service documentation. Expected: No external condition suggests compromised reliability. If impact, fluid intrusion, overheating, or significant damage is found, stop troubleshooting and escalate for repair evaluation.

steps.title: 14. Determine Whether the Failure Is Accessory-Related or Device-Related
steps.instructions: Review the results of all controlled substitutions and observations. Accessory-related failure is more likely when: A known-good electrode set resolves the problem; The original electrodes are damaged or expired; Analysis succeeds after correcting pad/contact conditions; The problem follows one specific electrode assembly. Device-related failure is more likely when: Multiple known-good compatible electrode sets fail; The approved simulator/test setup is verified; Power remains stable; Motion and interference have been ruled out; The analysis sequence repeatedly freezes or fails; Readiness or self-monitoring status is abnormal. Expected: The fault is isolated as far as possible without unnecessary internal disassembly. If the issue is resolved externally, complete all required post-service testing and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 powered on and delivered voice prompts but would not complete ECG rhythm analysis during use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced intermittent analysis failure with the original electrode assembly; analysis completed normally after installation of a known-good compatible electrode set.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the suspect electrode assembly, verified repeated analysis sequences using an approved AED simulator, confirmed ready status, and returned the device to service.

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Excessive Motion or CPR Interferes With Analysis
description: Troubleshooting repeated motion prompts, delayed rhythm analysis, or apparent CPR interference caused by movement, electrode contact, transport, configuration, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting during an active resuscitation event. During actual use, follow the LIFEPAK CR2 voice prompts, keep rescuers clear when instructed, and remove avoidable motion sources without delaying appropriate patient care. Expected: Patient care remains the priority, and troubleshooting is deferred until the device can be evaluated safely. Why it matters: Stryker states that the LIFEPAK CR2 motion-detection function can identify motion from CPR, rescuer movement, patient movement, or vehicle movement. Detected motion can inhibit ECG analysis and trigger a voice prompt. If the immediate clinical event is resolved, continue troubleshooting only in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Behavior
steps.instructions: Interview staff and determine whether the complaint involved: A repeated motion-related voice prompt; Analysis delayed while CPR continued; Analysis interrupted during patient transport; Rescuers touching or moving the patient; A stretcher, bed, or vehicle in motion; Analysis difficulty despite an apparently motionless test condition; A problem occurring during every use or only one event. Review available event information according to facility policy when appropriate. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to expected motion detection, an application-related problem, or a reproducible abnormal condition. Why it matters: A motion prompt during actual movement is not automatically evidence of AED failure. Stryker specifically identifies CPR, rescuer movement, patient movement, and vehicle movement as possible motion sources. If the reported behavior clearly matches unavoidable movement during the event and the unit otherwise operated normally, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the AED Before Testing
steps.instructions: Remove the device from clinical availability for controlled evaluation. Check for: Cracked or damaged enclosure; Evidence of impact or fluid intrusion; Damaged electrode connector area; Loose external components; Contamination around accessible contact areas; Abnormal readiness indication; Unusual heat, odor, or sound. Expected: The AED is externally intact and shows no obvious condition that could compromise safe operation. If physical damage, fluid intrusion, abnormal heat, or burning odor is found, stop testing, label the device Out of Service, and escalate for repair evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Verify Electrode Package and Connection Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the installed LIFEPAK CR2 electrode assembly and accessible connection path. Check for: Expired electrodes; Opened or damaged packaging; Dried or compromised pads; Loose connection; Damaged cable insulation; Bent, contaminated, or damaged accessible connection surfaces; Evidence that pads did not adhere fully during the reported event. Expected: Electrodes and their external connection are intact, in date, and properly connected. Why it matters: The CR2 analyzes ECG through the applied electrode system. Poor contact or unstable pad adhesion can contribute to a noisy or unreliable signal and should be excluded before suspecting an internal analysis fault. If replacing a questionable electrode set with an approved, compatible known-good set resolves the issue during controlled testing, restore the device only after required functional checks and stop.

steps.title: 5. Review Patient Motion and Rescuer Contact
steps.instructions: Determine whether motion occurred during the analysis period. Possible sources include: Active chest compressions; Ventilation-related body movement; Rescuer contact; Patient repositioning; Bed or stretcher movement; Ambulance or vehicle movement; Mechanical vibration. Expected: Any motion source is identified and correlated with the reported analysis interruption. Stryker states that when motion exceeds the system threshold, ECG analysis may be inhibited and the operator is advised by a voice prompt. The manufacturer also notes that motion can introduce ECG artifact. If the complaint occurred only while substantial movement was present and cannot be reproduced under stable conditions, document this as the likely cause and stop.

steps.title: 6. Distinguish Standard Analysis From cprINSIGHT Operation
steps.instructions: Determine the device configuration and whether the complaint is consistent with the expected analysis mode. On applicable LIFEPAK CR2 configurations, cprINSIGHT Analysis Technology is designed to analyze ECG rhythm while CPR is being performed. Stryker states that this feature can be configured on or off in advance and is intended to reduce pauses in compressions. Expected: Clinical Engineering confirms whether the observed behavior matches the configured analysis method. Why it matters: “CPR interferes with analysis” may reflect a misunderstanding of the AED’s configuration or sequence rather than a hardware defect. Do not change clinical configuration casually. Verify facility-approved settings and configuration-control requirements before making any change. If the configuration explains the reported behavior and controlled testing is normal, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 7. Verify Whether Motion Detection Is Configured as Expected
steps.instructions: Using the facility-approved configuration workflow, confirm whether motion detection is configured as intended. Stryker documents motion detection as a configurable function on applicable CR2 configurations. Compare the current setting with: Facility standard; Fleet configuration; Previously documented configuration; Approved clinical protocol. Expected: The device configuration matches the organization’s approved setup. Do not alter settings simply to suppress a reported prompt. Any configuration change should follow facility authorization and post-change verification requirements. If an unauthorized or incorrect configuration is found and correction resolves the complaint, document the change, complete required verification, and stop.

steps.title: 8. Reproduce the Complaint Under Stable Bench Conditions
steps.instructions: Using only approved test equipment and the organization’s authorized AED inspection process, evaluate the device in a stable environment. Ensure: AED remains stationary; Test setup is not being moved; Cables are not being pulled; No one touches the simulated patient connection during analysis; Test equipment connections remain secure. Expected: Analysis proceeds without repeated unexplained motion indications under a motion-free controlled condition. Why it matters: This separates expected motion response from a possible persistent sensing, electrode-path, or internal device problem. If the issue cannot be reproduced and all checks pass, document the controlled result and stop.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good Test Setup
steps.instructions: If repeated motion behavior persists, isolate external test variables one at a time. Where authorized and compatible, compare using: Known-good approved electrode/test interface; Known-good simulator connection setup; Stable alternate test surface; Another verified LIFEPAK CR2 for comparison. Change only one variable at a time. Expected: The failure follows either an external accessory/setup component or the suspect AED. If the problem follows an external component, replace or correct that component, repeat required testing, and stop when successful.

steps.title: 10. Check for Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Move testing away from potential sources of vibration or electrical interference. Examples include: Motorized beds; Compressors; Elevators; Large motors; Powered transport equipment; High-vibration carts; Poorly secured bench surfaces; Nearby equipment producing abnormal interference. Expected: The AED behaves consistently in a stable environment. If relocating the test setup resolves the problem, document the environmental cause and stop.

steps.title: 11. Perform the Approved Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After external causes are addressed, complete the facility-approved functional inspection appropriate to the LIFEPAK CR2. Verify, as applicable: Readiness status; Startup prompts; Electrode recognition; Analysis sequence; Motion-related behavior; Shock/no-shock test response using approved equipment; Final device status. Do not perform unapproved live shock testing or improvised patient simulation. Expected: The AED completes required functional verification without unexplained repeated motion detection or analysis failure. If the unit passes and the original complaint cannot be reproduced, return it to service only according to facility policy and document the findings.

steps.title: 12. Stop if Unexplained Analysis Interference Persists
steps.instructions: If repeated motion detection or analysis interruption continues when: The test setup is stationary; Approved connections are secure; Electrode-related causes are excluded; Environmental vibration is absent; Configuration is verified; do not assume normal operation. Expected: The device remains removed from service pending further evaluation. Persistent unexplained motion recognition may indicate a fault requiring authorized bench evaluation rather than further external troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 repeatedly issued a motion-related prompt and delayed rhythm analysis during CPR.
CCR.Cause: Controlled testing found the AED analyzed normally when stationary; event review indicated continued patient and stretcher movement during the reported analysis period.
CCR.Resolution: Inspected electrodes and external connections, verified approved device configuration, completed controlled functional testing successfully, and returned the AED to service.

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Shock Will Not Deliver
description: Troubleshooting failure to deliver an indicated shock caused by AED analysis state, electrode contact, depleted battery, accessories, controls, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting during an active cardiac arrest when the LIFEPAK CR2 is not delivering expected therapy. Immediately continue CPR according to the clinical response protocol and obtain another verified defibrillator/AED without delaying resuscitation. Expected: Patient care is transferred to functioning emergency equipment while resuscitation continues. Why it matters: A suspected therapy-delivery failure is a critical equipment condition. Troubleshooting must never delay CPR or access to another defibrillator. If another device restores access to defibrillation therapy, remove the affected LIFEPAK CR2 from clinical use and continue evaluation in a controlled Clinical Engineering environment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Whether a Shock Was Actually Advised
steps.instructions: Review the reported event carefully before concluding that the CR2 failed to deliver a shock. Determine whether the device: Announced that a shock was advised; Announced that no shock was advised; Continued CPR prompts without entering a shock sequence; Began charging but did not complete the sequence; Reached a shock-ready state but did not deliver therapy; Restarted, shut down, or produced an error during analysis or charging. Expected: Clinical Engineering distinguishes a true failure from normal AED operation when the analyzed rhythm does not meet the device’s criteria for shock therapy. Why it matters: An AED is not expected to shock every cardiac arrest rhythm. “No shock delivered” alone does not prove equipment failure. If the event was consistent with a normal “no shock advised” sequence and no device fault is present, document the findings and stop.

steps.title: 3. Identify the Device Configuration and Expected Shock Action
steps.instructions: Verify whether the specific LIFEPAK CR2 configuration is semi-automatic or fully automatic. For a semi-automatic configuration, confirm whether the expected user shock action occurred after the device reached the appropriate shock-ready sequence. For a fully automatic configuration, do not interpret the absence of a manual shock-button action as a defect. Expected: The reported behavior is compared with the actual configuration of the device. Why it matters: A configuration misunderstanding can be reported as “shock would not deliver” even when the unit is functioning as designed. If the complaint is explained by the device configuration, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check the Readiness Condition Before Further Testing
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK CR2 for its normal readiness indication and any attention condition. Check for: Missing normal readiness indication; Audible alert tones; Device-not-ready status; Visible damage; Signs of recent drop or impact; Evidence of fluid intrusion; Unusual heat; Burn odor or electrical smell. Expected: A ready-state device shows no unresolved attention condition or obvious physical damage. Why it matters: A device already indicating a readiness problem should not be trusted for therapy until the underlying condition is resolved. If abnormal heat, odor, liquid intrusion, or significant impact damage is present, stop testing, remove the unit from service, and escalate for evaluation.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the QUIK-STEP Electrode Assembly
steps.instructions: Verify that the installed electrode assembly is the correct compatible type for the LIFEPAK CR2. Check: Expiration date; Package integrity; Evidence the electrode package has been opened; Torn, punctured, or compromised packaging; Dried or contaminated adhesive gel; Damaged electrode leads; Physical damage to the tray or assembly; Signs the electrodes were previously deployed or used. Expected: The electrode assembly is compatible, within expiration, intact, and suitable for service. Why it matters: Damaged, expired, opened, or compromised electrodes can interfere with dependable patient contact and therapy readiness. If the electrode assembly is questionable, replace it with an approved compatible set, restore the unit to the proper ready condition, and reassess. If the issue is resolved, stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Electrode Contact as a Possible Cause of the Reported Event
steps.instructions: For an actual clinical event, determine from staff reports and available device/event information whether the CR2 repeatedly prompted for pad attachment or better contact. Ask whether: Pads were fully removed from their backing; Both pads were applied to the patient; Placement followed the device prompts; The chest was excessively wet; Heavy chest hair prevented adhesion; A pad lifted during CPR; Pads were placed over clothing; Movement disrupted contact. Expected: No evidence suggests that inadequate electrode contact prevented progression through analysis and therapy. Why it matters: Poor pad contact may interrupt rhythm analysis or prevent the device from progressing normally toward shock delivery. Do not attempt to reproduce a patient-contact problem on a person. Use only approved test methods in the Clinical Engineering environment. If pad contact explains the event and the device subsequently passes required evaluation, document the cause and stop.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Battery Installation and Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK CR2 lithium battery externally. Check for: Battery fully seated; Loose installation; Cracked housing; Swelling or deformation; Contamination at accessible contact areas; Corrosion; Evidence of leakage; Known replacement-due condition; Recent battery alert or replacement message. Reseat or replace the battery only according to the approved maintenance process using the correct compatible battery. Expected: The correct battery is secure, undamaged, and does not produce a low-battery or attention condition. Why it matters: Defibrillator charging requires dependable power. A degraded or poorly seated battery can contribute to startup, charging, or therapy-sequence problems. If an approved replacement battery restores normal readiness and the device passes required verification, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Power-Cycle Check
steps.instructions: In a controlled Clinical Engineering environment and after ensuring no patient is connected: Turn the device off. Inspect the battery and electrode installation. Restore the components correctly. Restart the device. Observe prompts, indicators, and any abnormal alert. Expected: The CR2 initializes normally without repeated fault indications or abnormal restart behavior. Why it matters: A controlled restart can identify a persistent startup or readiness fault without assuming internal failure. If the unit continues to indicate a fault, repeatedly restarts, or cannot reach a normal ready condition, stop and escalate.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Whether Charging Was the Actual Failure
steps.instructions: Review the reported sequence and determine whether the CR2: Never announced or indicated a shockable condition; Began a shock sequence but failed to become ready; Took abnormally long to progress; Restarted during charging; Produced a device fault; Became ready but then aborted the sequence. Expected: Clinical Engineering isolates the complaint to analysis, electrode contact, charging, user interaction, or actual energy delivery. Why it matters: “Would not shock” can describe several different failures. Correct isolation prevents unnecessary parts replacement and improves escalation documentation. If the device consistently fails during the charging portion of the sequence, remove it from service and proceed to authorized evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Inspect the External User Controls
steps.instructions: For configurations that use a manual shock action, inspect the accessible control area for: Cracking; Sticking; Contamination; Physical obstruction; Impact damage; Abnormal tactile response. Do not disassemble the control panel or attempt internal switch repair. Expected: External controls are intact and operate normally during approved functional evaluation. Why it matters: Physical damage or contamination can interfere with control actuation, but internal control repair is beyond external troubleshooting. If the control is mechanically abnormal or fails an approved functional check, remove the device from service and escalate.

steps.title: 11. Perform Approved Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Only qualified Clinical Engineering personnel should perform therapy verification using: An approved defibrillator analyzer or test load; Facility-approved procedures; Current manufacturer service information; The correct test setup for the specific CR2 configuration. Do not discharge the LIFEPAK CR2 into open air, loose electrodes, a person, or an improvised load. Verify, as permitted by the approved procedure: Normal startup; Readiness status; Electrode recognition; Analysis sequence; Charge progression; Shock sequence; Delivered-energy performance where authorized; Absence of device faults. Expected: The unit completes the approved verification sequence and meets applicable acceptance criteria. Why it matters: A reported shock-delivery failure cannot be safely cleared by visual inspection alone when therapy performance remains in question. If the device passes all required testing and the original complaint is explained by an external cause, document the findings and return it to service according to facility policy. If the failure is reproduced or results are questionable, stop.

steps.title: 12. Review Available Event and Device Information
steps.instructions: When available through the facility’s approved workflow, review relevant event data, service information, or AED program-management records. Look for evidence of: Shock advised versus no shock advised; Pad-contact interruptions; Battery warnings; Device-not-ready condition; Restart behavior; Fault indication; Incomplete therapy sequence. Expected: Objective device information supports or narrows the reported complaint. Why it matters: Event evidence may distinguish device failure from rhythm analysis, poor electrode contact, battery condition, or an incomplete user sequence. If the information identifies and resolves an external cause and the unit passes required verification, document and stop.

steps.title: 13. Make the Final Service Decision
steps.instructions: Return the LIFEPAK CR2 to service only when: The complaint has been explained or corrected; Correct compatible electrodes are installed; Battery condition is acceptable; No unresolved readiness alert exists; No physical safety concern remains; Required functional verification passes; Final status is documented. Expected: Only a verified, ready device is returned to emergency service. If any doubt remains about shock charging or therapy delivery, do not return the unit to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the LIFEPAK CR2 announced a shockable sequence but did not deliver the expected shock.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the installed QUIK-STEP electrode assembly compromised and the device could not complete the expected therapy sequence during initial evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the electrode assembly with an approved compatible set, restored normal readiness, completed approved functional verification, and confirmed acceptable operation before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Active patient event or bench complaint
Shock advised or no shock advised

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Voice Prompts, CPR Coaching, or Metronome Not Working
description: Troubleshooting missing, weak, intermittent, or unexpected voice prompts, CPR coaching, or metronome tones caused by startup, audio, configuration, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot missing audio guidance while the LIFEPAK CR2 is being relied upon during an active resuscitation. Immediately provide another verified AED/defibrillator when available and continue resuscitation according to the facility’s emergency-response procedures and trained responder protocols. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on a device with questionable audible guidance. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 uses audible instructions and CPR coaching to guide responders, including metronome tones at the intended compression rate. If another device resolves the immediate clinical concern, stop troubleshooting on the patient and evaluate the affected unit in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Mode
steps.instructions: Reproduce the complaint only in an approved controlled test environment and determine whether: No voice prompts are heard; Voice prompts are unusually faint; Audio is intermittent; Initial prompts work but CPR coaching does not; CPR coaching occurs but no metronome is heard; Adult guidance works differently than expected; Child-mode guidance is involved; The complaint occurs only at a particular stage of the rescue sequence; The device appears to stop progressing through the expected sequence. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to total audio failure, low/intermittent audio, sequence-specific behavior, or an expected configuration-dependent behavior. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 provides CPR coaching at appropriate points in the response sequence; not every prompt or metronome behavior is expected continuously. If the reported behavior is confirmed as normal sequence behavior, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Device Completes Normal Startup
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from clinical service for testing, activate it according to the approved facility test process. Observe for: Normal power-up behavior; Expected indicator activity; Audible startup instructions; Abnormal warning indications; Failure to progress beyond startup; Unexpected shutdown or reset. Expected: The device powers normally and begins its audible rescue guidance. If normal voice guidance returns and remains stable during the approved functional check, document the successful test and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check for Obstruction or Contamination Around the Audio Output Area
steps.instructions: Inspect the exterior of the device for anything that could reduce audible output, including: Tape; Labels; Dirt or debris; Dried cleaning residue; Fluid contamination; Carry-case material blocking an opening; Improper storage positioning. Do not insert objects into openings or use unapproved cleaning methods. Expected: External audio paths are unobstructed and the enclosure is clean and dry. Why it matters: A device producing normal audio internally may still appear abnormally quiet if its sound path is externally obstructed. If removing a safe, external obstruction restores normal audible operation, complete the approved functional check, document the correction, and stop.

steps.title: 5. Test in a Quiet Controlled Environment
steps.instructions: Repeat the approved operational check away from: Alarm-heavy clinical areas; Mechanical rooms; Running vehicles; High ambient conversation; Loud equipment. Listen for whether prompts are actually absent or simply difficult to hear. Expected: Voice prompts and tones can be evaluated without background noise masking the output. Why it matters: Stryker states that the LIFEPAK CR2 uses ClearVoice technology to adjust prompt volume based on ambient noise, so unusual environmental conditions may affect perceived loudness. If audio is normal in a controlled environment and no device fault is reproduced, document the environmental finding and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Complaint Occurs at the Correct Point in the Rescue Sequence
steps.instructions: Determine whether staff expected CPR coaching or metronome tones before the device had entered the relevant CPR interval. Using only an approved simulation or test method, verify whether the unit advances through the expected sequence. Expected: CPR coaching and metronome behavior occur during the appropriate portion of the rescue process rather than continuously. Why it matters: Stryker documentation describes CPR coaching as being provided at appropriate times, with metronome tones supporting chest-compression rate. If the device behaves normally when the full sequence is reproduced correctly, document “no fault found” with the observed test conditions and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check Adult and Child Mode Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint is associated with activation of child mode. Inspect the child-mode control for: Accidental activation; Sticking; Physical damage; Contamination; Unexpected indicator behavior. Repeat the approved controlled functional check in the applicable mode. Expected: Mode selection is deliberate, controls respond normally, and guidance is appropriate to the selected operating mode. Why it matters: The LIFEPAK CR2 provides adult and pediatric CPR guidance, and Stryker identifies dedicated child-mode functionality. If correcting an unintended mode selection resolves the complaint, complete functional verification, document the finding, and stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify CPR Coaching or Metronome Configuration
steps.instructions: Where the facility’s approved LIFEPAK CR2 management workflow permits configuration review, confirm the deployed settings against the organization’s intended configuration. Check for discrepancies involving: CPR metronome behavior; CPR timing or protocol configuration; Compression-to-ventilation sequence; Device configuration recently changed; Replacement or exchanged device loaded with different settings. Do not alter clinical configuration without authorization. Expected: Configuration matches the facility’s approved deployment standard. Why it matters: Stryker operating instructions identify configuration-dependent CPR metronome behavior; for example, specific prompts can depend on the selected CPR metronome setting. If an authorized configuration correction restores expected operation, verify the unit, document the exact setting discrepancy and correction, and stop.

steps.title: 9. Inspect the Enclosure and Controls for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Examine the device externally for: Cracked housing; Evidence of impact or drop damage; Loose enclosure sections; Liquid ingress evidence; Damaged controls; Abnormal deformation; Unusual heat or odor. Expected: No physical condition is found that could compromise dependable audio output or rescue operation. If significant damage, liquid ingress, unusual heat, or odor is present, stop testing immediately, remove the unit from service, and escalate for repair evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Compare With a Known-Good LIFEPAK CR2 When Available
steps.instructions: Using the same approved controlled test conditions, compare the affected unit with a known-good LIFEPAK CR2 of equivalent configuration. Compare: Startup prompt presence; Relative voice volume; Prompt timing; CPR coaching behavior; Metronome presence; Adult/child mode behavior. Expected: The affected unit performs comparably to the known-good unit. If the complaint exists only on the affected device, suspect a device-specific audio, control, configuration, or internal electronics fault. Do not proceed into speaker, amplifier, internal wiring, or board-level repair unless specifically authorized and trained under the manufacturer’s service process.

steps.title: 11. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the LIFEPAK CR2 to service, verify through the approved facility process that: Device readiness is acceptable; Startup behavior is normal; Voice prompts are audible; Expected CPR coaching is present; Expected metronome behavior is present; Controls respond correctly; No abnormal indicators remain; The original complaint cannot be reproduced. Expected: The LIFEPAK CR2 demonstrates dependable operation under controlled test conditions. If the issue is resolved and all required checks pass, return the unit according to facility policy, document the repair, and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the LIFEPAK CR2 powered on but CPR coaching and metronome tones were not heard during the expected CPR interval.
CCR.Cause: Controlled testing confirmed normal startup voice prompts, but the unit’s configuration differed from the facility-approved CPR metronome settings.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the authorized CPR configuration, repeated controlled functional testing, verified voice prompts and metronome operation, and returned the AED to service.

helpfulDetails: Returned to Service or Out of Service clearly recorded

title: Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Defibrillator - Wi-Fi or Cellular Connection Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed or intermittent Wi-Fi or cellular communication caused by signal, network access, configuration, location, account, or persistent device-side faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended connectivity troubleshooting while the LIFEPAK CR2 is required for emergency response or active patient care. Keep another verified AED immediately available if the affected unit’s overall readiness is uncertain. Do not delay defibrillation or patient care because of a wireless communication problem. Expected: Patient care remains supported by a ready, verified defibrillator. Why it matters: A connectivity failure may affect remote monitoring, readiness reporting, updates, or event-data transfer without necessarily proving that the AED’s therapy function has failed. Treat device readiness and network connectivity as separate concerns until verified. If the immediate safety concern is resolved, continue troubleshooting in a controlled Clinical Engineering environment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Mode
steps.instructions: Determine what staff or the AED management system is actually reporting. Check whether: Wi-Fi alone is failing; Cellular alone is failing; Both communication paths are unavailable; Communication is intermittent; The AED appears offline in LIFELINKcentral; The problem began after relocation; The problem began after a network or password change; Only one physical location is affected; Readiness information is stale rather than completely absent. Expected: The failure is narrowed to a specific communication path and symptom. If the issue is limited to one path while the alternate path communicates normally, document that distinction and troubleshoot only the affected path.

steps.title: 3. Verify Overall AED Readiness
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK CR2 for its normal readiness indication and check for any abnormal visual or audible condition. Confirm externally that: The device is not showing an obvious readiness fault; The battery is installed correctly; Required electrodes are present and connected as intended; There is no visible physical damage; There is no unusual heat, odor, moisture intrusion, or impact damage. Expected: The AED appears otherwise ready and the complaint remains isolated to connectivity. If the AED shows a separate readiness problem, remove it from service and address that condition before treating the issue as network-only.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Installed Connectivity Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that the specific LIFEPAK CR2 unit is actually equipped and configured for the communication method being tested. Do not assume every CR2 has identical connectivity capability. Confirm through available asset records, deployment documentation, or the organization’s AED management configuration whether the unit is expected to use: Wi-Fi; Cellular service; Both Wi-Fi and cellular connectivity. Expected: The tested communication method matches the unit’s actual configuration. If the unit was never provisioned for the reported connection method, correct the deployment record or escalate for proper configuration rather than diagnosing a hardware failure.

steps.title: 5. Check Physical Location and Signal Conditions
steps.instructions: Evaluate the AED at its normal installed location. For Wi-Fi, look for: Weak coverage; Recent relocation; Metal cabinets or enclosures; Basement or interior-room placement; Building renovations; Access-point changes; Large obstructions near the AED. For cellular-equipped units, look for: Poor indoor cellular coverage; Shielded rooms; Underground locations; Dense structural barriers; A recent move to a low-signal area. Stryker’s pre-implementation guidance specifically recommends checking Wi-Fi signal strength at the intended AED location with another wireless device. Expected: Adequate signal is available where the AED is deployed. If moving the AED temporarily to a known-good coverage area restores communication, stop. The likely cause is environmental coverage, not confirmed internal device failure.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Network Device
steps.instructions: At the same location, test the intended Wi-Fi network using an approved known-good device such as a facility-managed laptop, tablet, or phone. Confirm: The expected SSID is visible; The network is operational; Signal strength is reasonable; Other approved devices can communicate. Expected: The local wireless environment is verified independently of the AED. If other devices also fail, stop troubleshooting the CR2 and escalate the network problem to IT or the responsible infrastructure team.

steps.title: 7. Check for Recent Network Changes
steps.instructions: Ask IT or review change records for recent changes involving: SSID name; Wi-Fi password or security key; Authentication method; Access-point replacement; Network segmentation; Firewall rules; Internet access; Site relocation; Wireless security policy. Expected: The AED’s stored configuration remains compatible with the current network. If a network change occurred, update or reprovision the AED only through the approved Stryker-supported wireless setup process and facility change-control practices.

steps.title: 8. Verify Wi-Fi Network Compatibility and Access
steps.instructions: For a Wi-Fi complaint, confirm with IT that the intended network is appropriate for the LIFEPAK CR2 deployment. Check externally for: Correct network name; Correct credentials; Sufficient coverage; Internet access where required; No captive portal requiring browser acceptance; No unapproved access-control change blocking the device. Stryker provides a dedicated LIFEPAK CR2 wireless setup guide and recommends configuring Wi-Fi-capable units with a Wi-Fi network, including models that also have cellular capability. Expected: The intended Wi-Fi environment supports the configured AED connection. If IT identifies a network-side block, correct the infrastructure issue and retest before suspecting AED hardware.

steps.title: 9. Recheck the Approved Wireless Configuration
steps.instructions: Using the facility’s authorized process and Stryker’s supported wireless setup workflow, confirm that the unit is associated with the intended Wi-Fi configuration. Do not guess credentials or perform undocumented configuration changes. Check for: Wrong SSID; Outdated password; Configuration for a previous site; Incorrect deployment profile; Incomplete provisioning. Expected: The AED has the correct approved wireless configuration. If correcting the configuration restores communication, stop. Document the configuration mismatch and successful reconnection.

steps.title: 10. Determine Whether the Failure Is Location-Specific
